qa_pairs.question: What is the responsibility allocation requirement for effective implementation of KYC policies and procedures?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall allocate responsibility for effective implementation of policies and procedures.

qa_pairs.question: What is the requirement for independent evaluation of compliance functions?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall conduct independent evaluation of the compliance functions of REs’ policies and procedures, including legal and regulatory requirements.

qa_pairs.question: What is the requirement for a concurrent/internal audit system?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall have a concurrent/internal audit system to verify the compliance with KYC/AML policies and procedures.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities submit to the Audit Committee?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall submit quarterly audit notes and compliance to the Audit Committee.

qa_pairs.question: Under what condition is outsourcing of decision-making functions for determining compliance with KYC norms permitted?
qa_pairs.answer: Outsourcing of decision-making functions of determining compliance with KYC norms is not permitted.

qa_pairs.question: What is the requirement for submission of audit notes and compliance?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall submit quarterly audit notes and compliance to the Audit Committee.

qa_pairs.question: What is the frequency of submission of audit notes and compliance?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall submit quarterly audit notes and compliance to the Audit Committee.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when they are unable to apply appropriate CDD measures due to non-cooperation of the customer or non-reliability of the documents/information furnished by the customer?
qa_pairs.answer: The RE shall consider filing an STR, if necessary, when it is unable to comply with the relevant CDD measures in relation to the customer.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for undertaking a transaction or account-based relationship?
qa_pairs.answer: The CDD procedure must be followed.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is a fresh CDD exercise not required for an existing KYC compliant customer of a RE who desires to open another account or avail any other product or service from the same RE?
qa_pairs.answer: There shall be no need for a fresh CDD exercise as far as identification of the customer is concerned.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a customer permitted to act on behalf of another person/entity?
qa_pairs.answer: The circumstances in which a customer is permitted to act on behalf of another person/entity, is clearly spelt out.

qa_pairs.question: What system must be put in place to ensure that the identity of the customer does not match with any person or entity, whose name appears in the sanctions lists indicated in Chapter IX of this MD?
qa_pairs.answer: A suitable system is put in place.

qa_pairs.question: What must REs do when an equivalent e-document is obtained from the customer?
qa_pairs.answer: The RE shall verify the digital signature as per the provisions of the Information Technology Act, 2000 (21 of 2000).

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of the Customer Acceptance Policy?
qa_pairs.answer: The Customer Acceptance Policy shall not result in denial of banking/financial facility.

qa_pairs.question: What information must be verified from the verification facility of the issuing authority when a Permanent Account Number (PAN) is obtained?
qa_pairs.answer: The same shall be verified.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when rejecting an application for onboarding or periodic updation of KYC?
qa_pairs.answer: No application for onboarding or periodic updation of KYC shall be rejected without application of mind. Reason(s) of rejection shall be duly recorded by the officer concerned.

qa_pairs.question: What is the threshold for filing an STR with FIU-IND when performing the CDD process may tip-off the customer?
qa_pairs.answer: Where RE forms a suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing, and it reasonably believes that performing the CDD process will tip-off the customer, it shall not pursue the CDD process, and instead file an STR with FIU-IND.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the CDD process not required to be pursued?
qa_pairs.answer: Where RE forms a suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing, and it reasonably believes that performing the CDD process will tip-off the customer, it shall not pursue the CDD process, and instead file an STR with FIU-IND. However, this exception does not apply if the CDD process is not pursued.

qa_pairs.question: Who is considered a Person with Disabilities (PwD) for the purpose of this section?
qa_pairs.answer: PwDs are included in the list of members of the general public, especially those, who are financially or socially disadvantaged.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for filing an STR with FIU-IND when the CDD process may tip-off the customer?
qa_pairs.answer: Where RE forms a suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing, and it reasonably believes that performing the CDD process will tip-off the customer, it shall not pursue the CDD process, and instead file an STR with FIU-IND.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of recording reasons for rejection of KYC applications?
qa_pairs.answer: No application for onboarding or periodic updation of KYC shall be rejected without application of mind. Reason(s) of rejection shall be duly recorded by the officer concerned.

qa_pairs.question: What is the date of the circular that inserted section 11A?
qa_pairs.answer: Inserted vide circular DOR.AML.REC.111/14.01.001/2023-24 dated April 28, 2023.

qa_pairs.question: What is the consequence of not pursuing the CDD process when it may tip-off the customer?
qa_pairs.answer: Where RE forms a suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing, and it reasonably believes that performing the CDD process will tip-off the customer, it shall not pursue the CDD process, and instead file an STR with FIU-IND.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of including members of the general public, especially those, who are financially or socially disadvantaged, in this section?
qa_pairs.answer: members of the general public, especially those, who are financially or socially disadvantaged, including the Persons with Disabilities (PwDs) are included in this section.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when categorising customers?
qa_pairs.answer: Customers shall be categorised as low, medium and high-risk category, based on the assessment and risk perception of the RE.

qa_pairs.question: What parameters are considered for risk-categorisation of customers?
qa_pairs.answer: Risk categorisation shall be undertaken based on parameters such as customer’s identity, social/financial status, nature of business activity, and information about the customer’s business and their location, geographical risk covering customers as well as transactions, type of products/services offered, delivery channel used for delivery of products/services, types of transaction undertaken – cash, cheque/monetary instruments, wire transfers, forex transactions, etc.

qa_pairs.question: What information collected from customers relating to the perceived risk is permitted to be non-intrusive?
qa_pairs.answer: Various other information collected from different categories of customers relating to the perceived risk, is non-intrusive and the same is specified in the KYC policy.

qa_pairs.question: What shall be kept confidential in the risk categorisation process?
qa_pairs.answer: The risk categorisation of a customer and the specific reasons for such categorisation shall be kept confidential and shall not be revealed to the customer to avoid tipping off the customer.

qa_pairs.question: What may be used in risk assessment?
qa_pairs.answer: FATF Public Statement, the reports and guidance notes on KYC/AML issued by the Indian Banks Association (IBA), and other agencies, etc., may also be used in risk assessment.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of specifying the types of transactions undertaken in risk-categorisation?
qa_pairs.answer: The purpose is to cover types of transaction undertaken – cash, cheque/monetary instruments, wire transfers, forex transactions, etc.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for undertaking risk-categorisation of customers?
qa_pairs.answer: Risk categorisation shall be undertaken based on parameters such as customer’s identity, social/financial status, nature of business activity, and information about the customer’s business and their location, geographical risk covering customers as well as transactions, type of products/services offered, delivery channel used for delivery of products/services, types of transaction undertaken – cash, cheque/monetary instruments, wire transfers, forex transactions, etc.

qa_pairs.question: What is the basis for risk-categorisation of customers?
qa_pairs.answer: Risk categorisation shall be undertaken based on assessment and risk perception of the RE.

qa_pairs.question: What is the principle that may be laid down by the REs for risk-categorisation of customers?
qa_pairs.answer: Broad principles may be laid down by the REs for risk-categorisation of customers.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when there is a doubt about the authenticity or adequacy of the customer identification data it has obtained?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities must ensure that the customer identification data is verified and confirmed before proceeding with the transaction.

qa_pairs.question: What is the monetary limit for selling third party products as agents, selling their own products, payment of dues of credit cards/sale and reloading of prepaid/travel cards?
qa_pairs.answer: The monetary limit is rupees fifty thousand.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the requirement to verify the identity of customers not applicable?
qa_pairs.answer: The requirement to verify the identity of customers is not applicable when introduction is not sought while opening accounts.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a customer for the purpose of verifying the identity at the time of opening an account?
qa_pairs.answer: For the purpose of verifying the identity of customers at the time of opening an account, the term customer includes both account-based and walk-in customers.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for verifying the identity of customers at the time of opening an account?
qa_pairs.answer: The procedure for verifying the identity of customers at the time of opening an account is not explicitly stated in this section, but regulated entities must ensure that the customer identification data is verified and confirmed before proceeding with the transaction.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when carrying out any international money transfer operations for a person who is not an account holder of the RE?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities must ensure that the customer identification data is verified and confirmed before proceeding with the transaction.

qa_pairs.question: What is the monetary limit for carrying out transactions for a non-account-based customer, that is a walk-in customer?
qa_pairs.answer: The monetary limit is rupees fifty thousand.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the requirement to verify the identity of customers not applicable when there is a doubt about the authenticity or adequacy of the customer identification data?
qa_pairs.answer: The requirement to verify the identity of customers is not applicable when introduction is not sought while opening accounts.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when a RE has reason to believe that a customer (account-based or walk-in) is intentionally structuring a transaction into a series of transactions below the threshold of rupees fifty thousand?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities must ensure that the customer identification data is verified and confirmed before proceeding with the transaction.

qa_pairs.question: What must REs do when relying on customer due diligence done by a third party?
qa_pairs.answer: REs shall at their option, rely on customer due diligence done by a third party, subject to the conditions specified in Section 14.

qa_pairs.question: What is the monetary limit for relying on customer due diligence done by a third party?
qa_pairs.answer: The monetary limit is rupees fifty thousand, whether conducted as a single transaction or several transactions that appear to be connected, or any international money transfer operations.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is a third party permitted to be based in a country or jurisdiction?
qa_pairs.answer: A third party shall not be based in a country or jurisdiction assessed as high risk.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a regulated third party for the purpose of customer due diligence?
qa_pairs.answer: A third party that is regulated, supervised or monitored for, and has measures in place for, compliance with customer due diligence and record-keeping requirements in line with the requirements and obligations under the PML Act.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for obtaining records or information of customer due diligence carried out by a third party?
qa_pairs.answer: Records or the information of the customer due diligence carried out by the third party is obtained immediately from the third party or from the Central KYC Records Registry.

qa_pairs.question: What must REs do to satisfy themselves that copies of identification data and other relevant documentation are available from a third party?
qa_pairs.answer: Adequate steps are taken by REs to satisfy themselves that copies of identification data and other relevant documentation relating to the customer due diligence are made available from the third party upon request without delay.

qa_pairs.question: What is the ultimate responsibility for customer due diligence and undertaking enhanced due diligence measures?
qa_pairs.answer: The ultimate responsibility for customer due diligence and undertaking enhanced due diligence measures, as applicable, will be with the RE.

qa_pairs.question: What must REs do to ensure that a third party has measures in place for compliance with customer due diligence and record-keeping requirements?
qa_pairs.answer: REs must ensure that the third party is regulated, supervised or monitored for, and has measures in place for, compliance with customer due diligence and record-keeping requirements in line with the requirements and obligations under the PML Act.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for requesting records or information of customer due diligence carried out by a third party?
qa_pairs.answer: Records or the information of the customer due diligence carried out by the third party is obtained immediately from the third party or from the Central KYC Records Registry, and the third party shall make available the records or information upon request without delay.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when an individual submits their Aadhaar number voluntarily?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall carry out authentication of the customer's Aadhaar number using e-KYC authentication facility provided by the Unique Identification Authority of India.

qa_pairs.question: What is the monetary/time limit for Aadhaar-based e-KYC authentication?
qa_pairs.answer: There is no specific monetary/time limit mentioned in the section for Aadhaar-based e-KYC authentication.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is offline verification not required for Aadhaar-based e-KYC authentication?
qa_pairs.answer: Offline verification is not required when the customer submits an equivalent e-document of any OVD, or when the customer provides a KYC Identifier with an explicit consent to download records from CKYCR.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a customer who can submit a proof of possession of Aadhaar Number containing Aadhaar Number?
qa_pairs.answer: A customer who submits a proof of possession of Aadhaar Number containing Aadhaar Number, where the authentication of Aadhaar number is not required, is eligible to submit such proof.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for carrying out offline verification for Aadhaar-based e-KYC authentication?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall carry out offline verification when the customer submits a proof of possession of Aadhaar under clause (aa) above where offline verification can be carried out.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when a customer submits a certified copy of the proof of possession of Aadhaar number or the OVD?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall verify the digital signature as per the provisions of the Information Technology Act, 2000 and any rules issued thereunder and take a live photo as specified under Annex I.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for retrieving KYC records online from the CKYCR?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall retrieve the KYC records online from the CKYCR in accordance with paragraph 56, when the customer submits a KYC Identifier under clause (ac) above.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is digital KYC not required for Aadhaar-based e-KYC authentication?
qa_pairs.answer: Digital KYC is not required for a period not beyond such date as may be notified by the Government for a class of regulated entities, instead of carrying out digital KYC, the RE pertaining to such class may obtain a certified copy of the proof of possession of Aadhaar number or the OVD and a recent photograph.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when a customer wants to provide a current address, different from the address as per the identity information available in the Central Identities Data Repository?
qa_pairs.answer: The customer may give a self-declaration to that effect to the regulated entity.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when a customer requests a change of mobile number in an OTP-based e-KYC account?
qa_pairs.answer: REs shall have a board-approved policy delineating a robust process of due diligence for dealing with such requests.

qa_pairs.question: What is the threshold for the aggregate balance of all deposit accounts of a customer?
qa_pairs.answer: The aggregate balance shall not exceed rupees one lakh.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is an OTP-based e-KYC account not allowed for more than one year?
qa_pairs.answer: Unless identification as per paragraph 16 or as per paragraph 18 (V-CIP) is carried out, OTP-based e-KYC accounts shall not be allowed for more than one year.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a customer for the purpose of OTP-based e-KYC?
qa_pairs.answer: The section does not provide a definition of a customer for OTP-based e-KYC, but it is implied that the customer must be an individual.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for completing CDD for OTP-based e-KYC accounts that have exceeded the balance threshold?
qa_pairs.answer: The account shall cease to be operational until CDD is complete.

qa_pairs.question: What is the maximum aggregate amount of term loans that can be sanctioned to a customer in a year?
qa_pairs.answer: The aggregate amount of term loans sanctioned shall not exceed rupees sixty thousand in a year.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do to ensure compliance with the conditions for OTP-based e-KYC accounts?
qa_pairs.answer: REs shall have strict monitoring procedures including systems to generate alerts in case of any non-compliance/violation.

qa_pairs.question: What is the consequence of not completing CDD for OTP-based e-KYC accounts within a year?
qa_pairs.answer: In respect of deposit accounts, the same shall be closed immediately. In respect of borrowal accounts, no further debits shall be allowed.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when undertaking V-CIP for a proprietorship firm?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall also obtain the equivalent e-document of the activity proofs with respect to the proprietorship firm, apart from undertaking CDD of the proprietor.

qa_pairs.question: What is the monetary/time limit for using Aadhaar XML file or Aadhaar QR code for offline verification of Aadhaar?
qa_pairs.answer: The XML file or QR code generation date must not be older than three working days from the date of carrying out V-CIP.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the use of printed copy of equivalent e-document including e-PAN not valid for V-CIP?
qa_pairs.answer: The use of printed copy of equivalent e-document including e-PAN is not valid for V-CIP. However, e-PAN provided by the customer is an exception.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a Business Correspondent (BC) assisting the customer in V-CIP?
qa_pairs.answer: Business Correspondents (BCs) facilitating the process only at the customer end qualify as BCs assisting the customer in V-CIP.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for capturing a clear image of PAN card during V-CIP?
qa_pairs.answer: The authorised official of the RE shall capture a clear image of PAN card to be displayed by the customer during the process, except in cases where e-PAN is provided by the customer.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when undertaking V-CIP for a new customer on-boarding for individual customers?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities must undertake CDD in case of new customer on-boarding for individual customers.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for ensuring that the video process of the V-CIP is undertaken within three working days of downloading/obtaining the identification information through CKYCR/Aadhaar authentication/equivalent e-document?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall ensure that the video process of the V-CIP is undertaken within three working days of downloading/obtaining the identification information through CKYCR/Aadhaar authentication/equivalent e-document, if in the rare cases, the entire process cannot be completed at one go or seamlessly.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when undertaking V-CIP for a Legal Entity (LE) customer?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities must undertake CDD of authorised signatories and Beneficial Owners (BOs) in case of Legal Entity (LE) customers.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for ensuring that the photograph of the customer in the Aadhaar/OVD and PAN/e-PAN matches with the customer undertaking the V-CIP?
qa_pairs.answer: The authorised official of the RE shall ensure that photograph of the customer in the Aadhaar/OVD and PAN/e-PAN matches with the customer undertaking the V-CIP.

qa_pairs.question: What are the limitations on a Small Account?
qa_pairs.answer: The aggregate of all credits in a financial year does not exceed rupees one lakh, the aggregate of all withdrawals and transfers in a month does not exceed rupees ten thousand, and the balance at any point of time does not exceed rupees fifty thousand.

qa_pairs.question: What must banks obtain from a customer opening a Small Account?
qa_pairs.answer: A self-attested photograph from the customer.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the limit on balance not considered for deposits?
qa_pairs.answer: Deposits through Government grants, welfare benefits, and payment against procurements.

qa_pairs.question: What is the maximum amount that can be withdrawn or transferred from a Small Account in a month?
qa_pairs.answer: Rupees ten thousand.

qa_pairs.question: What is the maximum balance allowed in a Small Account at any point of time?
qa_pairs.answer: Rupees fifty thousand.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for a prisoner to open a Small Account?
qa_pairs.answer: The signature or thumb print shall be affixed in presence of the officer in-charge of the jail and the said officer shall certify the same under his signature, and the account shall remain operational on annual submission of certificate of proof of address issued by the officer in-charge of the jail.

qa_pairs.question: What must the designated officer of the bank certify for a Small Account?
qa_pairs.answer: That the person opening the account has affixed his signature or thumb impression in his presence.

qa_pairs.question: What is the maximum amount that can be credited to a Small Account in a financial year?
qa_pairs.answer: Rupees one lakh.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when a customer expresses inability to complete the documentation requirements?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall, at their option, complete the verification of identity of the customer within a period of six months from the date of establishment of the relationship.

qa_pairs.question: What is the period for which a small account shall remain operational initially?
qa_pairs.answer: The account shall remain operational initially for a period of twelve months.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the requirement to obtain one of the six OVDs not applicable for a customer?
qa_pairs.answer: The requirement to obtain one of the six OVDs is not applicable for a customer who is categorised as ‘low risk’ and is applying the simplified procedure.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a customer for whom the simplified procedure is applied?
qa_pairs.answer: Customers who are categorised as ‘low risk’ qualify as customers for whom the simplified procedure is applied.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for monitoring a small account?
qa_pairs.answer: The account shall be monitored and when there is suspicion of money laundering or financing of terrorism activities or other high-risk scenarios, the identity of the customer shall be established as per paragraph 16 or paragraph a.

qa_pairs.question: What must banks ensure before a transaction is allowed to take place in a small account?
qa_pairs.answer: Banks shall ensure that the stipulated monthly and annual limits on aggregate of transactions and balance requirements in such accounts are not breached.

qa_pairs.question: What is the period after which the entire relaxation provisions for a small account shall be reviewed?
qa_pairs.answer: The entire relaxation provisions shall be reviewed after twenty-four months.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the small account not required to be operational between April 1, 2020 and June 30, 2020 and such other periods as may be notified by the Central Government?
qa_pairs.answer: The small account is not required to be operational between April 1, 2020 and June 30, 2020 and such other periods as may be notified by the Central Government.

qa_pairs.question: What is the maximum period for which a small account can be extended?
qa_pairs.answer: The account can be extended for a further period of twelve months, provided the account holder applies and furnishes evidence of having applied for any of the OVDs during the first twelve months of the opening of the said account.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when crediting foreign remittance into a customer's account?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities must ensure the identity of the customer is fully established as per paragraph 16 or paragraph 18.

qa_pairs.question: What is the condition for allowing foreign remittance to be credited into a customer's account?
qa_pairs.answer: Foreign remittance shall not be allowed to be credited into the account unless the identity of the customer is fully established as per paragraph 16 or paragraph 18.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the identity of the customer not required to be established for foreign remittance?
qa_pairs.answer: The identity of the customer is not required to be established if the remittance is being credited into an account that has already been established as per paragraph 16 or paragraph 18.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a customer whose identity must be established for foreign remittance?
qa_pairs.answer: Any customer receiving foreign remittance must have their identity fully established as per paragraph 16 or paragraph 18.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for crediting foreign remittance into a customer's account?
qa_pairs.answer: The procedure for crediting foreign remittance involves ensuring the identity of the customer is fully established as per paragraph 16 or paragraph 18, and then allowing the remittance to be credited into the account.

qa_pairs.question: What paragraphs must regulated entities refer to for establishing the identity of a customer for foreign remittance?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities must refer to paragraph 16 or paragraph 18 for establishing the identity of a customer for foreign remittance.

qa_pairs.question: Is it mandatory to establish the identity of a customer for foreign remittance?
qa_pairs.answer: Yes, it is mandatory to establish the identity of a customer for foreign remittance as per paragraph 18.

qa_pairs.question: What happens if the identity of the customer is not established for foreign remittance?
qa_pairs.answer: Foreign remittance shall not be allowed to be credited into the account unless the identity of the customer is fully established as per paragraph 16 or paragraph 18.

qa_pairs.question: What must NBFCs do when a customer desires to open an account but cannot produce documents?
qa_pairs.answer: NBFCs may open accounts subject to the conditions specified in paragraph 24. S.

qa_pairs.question: What is the monetary limit for balances in all accounts taken together?
qa_pairs.answer: The balances shall not exceed rupees fifty thousand at any point of time.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the full KYC procedure not required to be completed immediately?
qa_pairs.answer: The full KYC procedure is not required to be completed immediately if the customer is made aware that no further transactions will be permitted until the full KYC procedure is completed in case Directions (d) and (e) above are breached by him.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a customer under paragraph 24. S?
qa_pairs.answer: A person who desires to open an account is considered a customer under paragraph 24. S.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for monitoring accounts under paragraph 24. S?
qa_pairs.answer: The account shall be monitored and when there is suspicion of ML/TF activities or other high-risk scenarios, the identity of the customer shall be established as per paragraph 16 or paragraph 18.

qa_pairs.question: What is the monetary limit for total credit in all accounts taken together in a year?
qa_pairs.answer: The total credit shall not exceed rupees one lakh in a year.

qa_pairs.question: What must the customer be notified when the balance reaches rupees forty thousand or the total credit in a year reaches rupees eighty thousand?
qa_pairs.answer: The customer shall be notified that appropriate documents for conducting the KYC must be submitted otherwise the operations in the account shall be stopped when the total balance in all the accounts taken together exceeds the limits prescribed in direction (d) and (e) above.

qa_pairs.question: What is the initial operational period for accounts opened under paragraph 24. S?
qa_pairs.answer: The account shall remain operational initially for a period of twelve months, within which CDD as per paragraph 16 or paragraph 18 shall be carried out.

qa_pairs.question: What must the designated officer of the NBFC certify under his signature?
qa_pairs.answer: The designated officer of the NBFC certifies under his signature that the person opening the account has affixed his signature or thumb impression in his presence.

qa_pairs.question: What must a regulated entity do before transferring an account to another branch/office?
qa_pairs.answer: The regulated entity must ensure that full KYC verification has already been done for the concerned account and the periodic updation of the same is not due.

qa_pairs.question: What is the condition for transferring an account to another branch/office?
qa_pairs.answer: The account transfer is permitted only if full KYC verification has already been done for the concerned account and the periodic updation of the same is not due.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of KYC verification for account transfer?
qa_pairs.answer: The purpose of KYC verification is to ensure that the account holder's identity and address have been verified and updated, if necessary, before transferring the account to another branch/office.

qa_pairs.question: What is the process for transferring an account to another branch/office?
qa_pairs.answer: The process for transferring an account to another branch/office involves ensuring that full KYC verification has already been done for the concerned account and the periodic updation of the same is not due, and then transferring the account to the new branch/office.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when a customer's KYC information has not changed?

qa_pairs.question: What is the minimum periodicity for updation of KYC for high-risk customers?

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the requirement of positive confirmation for address verification not required?
qa_pairs.answer: The requirement of positive confirmation for address verification is not required when Aadhaar OTP based e-KYC in non-face to face mode is used for updation/ periodic updation. qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a low-risk customer for the purpose of KYC updation?
qa_pairs.answer: Low-risk customers are those who are categorized as low risk. Under Section 38.U, in respect of an individual customer who is categorized as low risk, the RE shall allow all transactions and ensure the updation of KYC within one year of its falling due for KYC or upto June 30, 2026, whichever is later.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for completing V-CIP for KYC updation?
qa_pairs.answer: The procedure for completing V-CIP for KYC updation is not specified in this section. qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when a customer's PAN details are available with them?

qa_pairs.question: What is the time limit for customers to submit updated documents to regulated entities?
qa_pairs.answer: Customers shall submit to the REs the update of such documents within 30 days of the update to the documents for the purpose of updating the records at REs’ end. qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when a customer's KYC details are not updated in time?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall give at least three reminders, including at least one reminder by letter, at appropriate intervals, to such customers who have still not complied with the requirements, despite advance intimations. Under Section 38.U, the RE shall give at least three reminders, including at least one reminder by letter, at appropriate intervals, to such customers who have still not complied with the requirements, despite advance intimations.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when an existing customer fails to submit a Permanent Account Number or equivalent e-document?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall temporarily cease operations in the account till the time the Permanent Account Number or equivalent e-documents thereof or Form No. 60 is submitted by the customer.

qa_pairs.question: What is the deadline for existing customers to submit a Permanent Account Number or equivalent e-document?
qa_pairs.answer: The deadline is such date as may be notified by the Central Government.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is a regulated entity not required to temporarily cease operations for an account?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities are not required to temporarily cease operations for an account if the customer is unable to provide Permanent Account Number or equivalent e-document due to injury, illness, or infirmity on account of old age or otherwise, and such like causes. However, such accounts shall be subject to enhanced monitoring.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a customer unable to provide Permanent Account Number or equivalent e-document due to injury, illness, or infirmity on account of old age or otherwise?

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for temporarily ceasing operations for an account?
qa_pairs.answer: Before temporarily ceasing operations for an account, the regulated entity shall give the customer an accessible notice and a reasonable opportunity to be heard.

qa_pairs.question: What must a regulated entity do if a customer gives in writing that they do not want to submit their Permanent Account Number or equivalent e-document?
qa_pairs.answer: The regulated entity shall close the account and all obligations due in relation to the account shall be appropriately settled after establishing the identity of the customer by obtaining the identification documents as applicable to the customer.

qa_pairs.question: What is the meaning of 'temporary ceasing of operations' in relation to an account?
qa_pairs.answer: For the purpose of this paragraph, ‘temporary ceasing of operations’ in relation to an account shall mean the temporary suspension of all transactions or activities in relation to that account by the RE till such time the customer complies with the provisions of this paragraph.

qa_pairs.question: What type of accounts are exempt from the rule of only allowing credits during temporary ceasing of operations?
qa_pairs.answer: Asset accounts such as loan accounts are exempt from the rule of only allowing credits during temporary ceasing of operations.

qa_pairs.question: What must a regulated entity do after temporarily ceasing operations for an account?
qa_pairs.answer: The regulated entity shall allow credits in the account during the temporary ceasing of operations, except for asset accounts such as loan accounts.

qa_pairs.question: What must REs do when introducing the process of V-CIP for remote onboarding?
qa_pairs.answer: The RE shall provide V-CIP as the first option to the customer for remote onboarding. Processes complying with prescribed standards and procedures for V-CIP shall be treated on par with face-to-face CIP for the purpose of this Master Direction.

qa_pairs.question: What is the threshold for linking alternate mobile numbers for transaction OTP, transaction updates, etc.?
qa_pairs.answer: Alternate mobile numbers shall not be linked post CDD with such accounts for transaction OTP, transaction updates, etc.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is it not required to obtain a positive confirmation of the current address through means such as address verification letter, contact point verification, deliverables, etc.?
qa_pairs.answer: It is not required to obtain a positive confirmation of the current address when the address proof is obtained from a certifying authority as allowed for NRIs and PIOs.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a high-risk customer for non-face-to-face customer onboarding?
qa_pairs.answer: Such customers shall be categorized as high-risk customers and accounts opened in non-face to face mode shall be subjected to enhanced monitoring until the identity of the customer is verified in face-to-face manner or through V-CIP.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for allowing operations in the account for non-face-to-face customer onboarding?
qa_pairs.answer: RE shall verify the current address through positive confirmation before allowing operations in the account. Positive confirmation may be carried out by means such as address verification letter, contact point verification, deliverables, etc.

qa_pairs.question: What document must REs obtain from the customer for non-face-to-face customer onboarding?
qa_pairs.answer: RE shall obtain PAN from the customer and the PAN shall be verified from the verification facility of the issuing authority.

qa_pairs.question: What is the first transaction requirement for non-face-to-face customer onboarding?
qa_pairs.answer: First transaction in such accounts shall be a credit from existing KYC-complied bank account of the customer.

qa_pairs.question: What is the process for dealing with requests for change of registered mobile number for non-face-to-face customer onboarding?
qa_pairs.answer: RE shall have a Board approved policy delineating a robust process of due diligence for dealing with requests for change of registered mobile number.

qa_pairs.question: What is the requirement for accounts opened in non-face to face mode for non-face-to-face customer onboarding?
qa_pairs.answer: Accounts opened in non-face to face mode shall be subjected to enhanced monitoring until the identity of the customer is verified in face-to-face manner or through V-CIP.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when dealing with a customer who is a Politically Exposed Person?
qa_pairs.answer: Apart from performing normal customer due diligence, REs must have in place appropriate risk management systems to determine whether the customer or the beneficial owner is a PEP, take reasonable measures for establishing the source of funds/wealth, obtain senior management approval to open an account, subject all such accounts to enhanced monitoring on an on-going basis, and obtain senior management approval to continue the business relationship if the customer or beneficial owner subsequently becomes a PEP.

qa_pairs.question: What is the approval requirement for opening an account for a Politically Exposed Person?
qa_pairs.answer: The approval to open an account for a PEP shall be obtained from the senior management.

qa_pairs.question: What is the definition of a Politically Exposed Person?
qa_pairs.answer: For the purpose of this paragraph, “Politically Exposed Persons” (PEPs) are individuals who are or have been entrusted with prominent public functions, including the Heads of States/Governments, senior politicians, senior government or judicial or military officers, senior executives of state-owned corporations and important political party officials.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is enhanced monitoring not required for a Politically Exposed Person account?
qa_pairs.answer: None specified; all such accounts are subjected to enhanced monitoring on an on-going basis.

qa_pairs.question: What must REs do to determine whether a customer or beneficial owner is a Politically Exposed Person?
qa_pairs.answer: REs must have in place appropriate risk management systems to determine whether the customer or the beneficial owner is a PEP.

qa_pairs.question: What is the requirement for establishing the source of funds/wealth for a Politically Exposed Person?
qa_pairs.answer: Reasonable measures must be taken by the REs for establishing the source of funds/wealth.

qa_pairs.question: What is the process for continuing a business relationship with a customer who becomes a Politically Exposed Person?
qa_pairs.answer: Senior management’s approval is required to continue the business relationship if the customer or beneficial owner subsequently becomes a PEP.

qa_pairs.question: Are family members or close associates of Politically Exposed Persons subject to these instructions?
qa_pairs.answer: Yes, these instructions shall also be applicable to family members or close associates of PEPs.

qa_pairs.question: What must REs ensure when opening client accounts through professional intermediaries?
qa_pairs.answer: REs shall ensure that clients are identified when client account is opened by a professional intermediary on behalf of a single client.

qa_pairs.question: What is the option available to REs for holding accounts managed by professional intermediaries?
qa_pairs.answer: REs shall have the option to hold 'pooled' accounts managed by professional intermediaries on behalf of entities like mutual funds, pension funds or other types of funds.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions are professional intermediaries not permitted to open accounts?
qa_pairs.answer: REs shall not open accounts of such professional intermediaries who are bound by any client confidentiality that prohibits disclosure of the client details to the RE.

qa_pairs.question: Who must be identified when funds held by intermediaries are not co-mingled at the level of RE?
qa_pairs.answer: All the beneficial owners shall be identified where funds held by the intermediaries are not co-mingled at the level of RE, and there are 'sub-accounts', each of them attributable to a beneficial owner.

qa_pairs.question: What is the condition for REs to rely on the CDD done by an intermediary?
qa_pairs.answer: REs shall, at their discretion, rely on the 'customer due diligence' (CDD) done by an intermediary, provided that the intermediary is a regulated and supervised entity and has adequate systems in place to comply with the KYC requirements of the customers.

qa_pairs.question: Who bears the ultimate responsibility for knowing the customer?
qa_pairs.answer: The ultimate responsibility for knowing the customer lies with the RE.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for identifying beneficial owners when funds are co-mingled at the level of RE?
qa_pairs.answer: The RE shall look for the beneficial owners where such funds are co-mingled at the level of RE.

qa_pairs.question: What is the condition for REs to hold 'pooled' accounts managed by professional intermediaries?
qa_pairs.answer: REs shall have the option to hold 'pooled' accounts managed by professional intermediaries on behalf of entities like mutual funds, pension funds or other types of funds.

qa_pairs.question: What is the threshold for identifying beneficial owners when funds are not co-mingled at the level of RE?
qa_pairs.answer: There are 'sub-accounts', each of them attributable to a beneficial owner.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when opening a savings bank account for a Self Help Group (SHG)?
qa_pairs.answer: The CDD of all the office bearers shall suffice.

qa_pairs.question: What is the threshold for CDD of SHG members?
qa_pairs.answer: CDD of all the members of SHG shall not be required while opening the savings bank account of the SHG.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is CDD of all SHG members not required?
qa_pairs.answer: CDD of all the members of SHG shall not be required while opening the savings bank account of the SHG.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as an office bearer of an SHG?
qa_pairs.answer: The CDD of all the office bearers shall suffice.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for undertaking CDD of SHG members?
qa_pairs.answer: CDD of all the members of SHG may be undertaken at the time of credit linking of SHGs.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of CDD of office bearers of an SHG?
qa_pairs.answer: The CDD of all the office bearers shall suffice.

qa_pairs.question: When can CDD of SHG members be undertaken?
qa_pairs.answer: CDD of all the members of SHG may be undertaken at the time of credit linking of SHGs.

qa_pairs.question: Is CDD of all SHG members required for credit linking of SHGs?
qa_pairs.answer: CDD of all the members of SHG may be undertaken at the time of credit linking of SHGs.

qa_pairs.question: What must banks do at their option when opening a Non-Resident Ordinary (NRO) bank account for a foreign student?
qa_pairs.answer: Banks shall open a Non-Resident Ordinary (NRO) bank account of a foreign student on the basis of his/her passport (with visa & immigration endorsement) bearing the proof of identity and address in the home country together with a photograph and a letter offering admission from the educational institution in India.

qa_pairs.question: What is the monetary limit for foreign remittances into the account during the 30-day period before address verification?
qa_pairs.answer: USD 1,000 or equivalent

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the address verification not required within 30 days of opening the account?
qa_pairs.answer: The address verification is not required within 30 days of opening the account, but a declaration about the local address must be obtained within this period.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a foreign student for the purpose of opening an NRO account?
qa_pairs.answer: A foreign student who has been offered admission from an educational institution in India.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for operating the account pending the verification of address?
qa_pairs.answer: The account shall be operated with a condition of allowing foreign remittances not exceeding USD 1,000 or equivalent into the account and a cap of rupees fifty thousand on aggregate in the same, during the 30-day period.

qa_pairs.question: What is the time limit for obtaining a declaration about the local address after opening the account?
qa_pairs.answer: Within a period of 30 days of opening the account.

qa_pairs.question: What is the monetary limit for aggregate transactions in the account during the 30-day period before address verification?
qa_pairs.answer: Rupees fifty thousand

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is prior approval of the Reserve Bank required for opening the account?
qa_pairs.answer: Students with Pakistani nationality shall require prior approval of the Reserve Bank for opening the account.

qa_pairs.question: What are the Reserve Bank of India’s instructions that the account shall be operated in terms of?
qa_pairs.answer: Reserve Bank of India’s instructions on Non-Resident Ordinary Rupee (NRO) Account, and the provisions of FEMA 1999.

qa_pairs.question: What must banks do when opening an account for a Foreign Portfolio Investor (FPI)?
qa_pairs.answer: Banks shall open accounts of FPIs by accepting KYC documents as detailed in Annex IV, subject to Income Tax (FATCA/CRS) Rules.

qa_pairs.question: What is the threshold for FPIs to be eligible for simplified KYC norms?
qa_pairs.answer: FPIs which are eligible/registered as per SEBI guidelines are eligible for simplified KYC norms.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the submission of exempted documents not required from FPIs?
qa_pairs.answer: The submission of exempted documents is not required from FPIs when the documents are submitted as and when required, as per the undertaking obtained from the FPI or the Global Custodian acting on behalf of the FPI.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a Foreign Portfolio Investor (FPI) eligible for simplified KYC norms?
qa_pairs.answer: FPIs which are eligible/registered as per SEBI guidelines qualify as FPIs eligible for simplified KYC norms.

qa_pairs.question: What documents are required from FPIs for KYC purposes?
qa_pairs.answer: KYC documents as detailed in Annex IV are required from FPIs for KYC purposes.

qa_pairs.question: What is the process for obtaining an undertaking from FPIs or the Global Custodian acting on behalf of the FPI?
qa_pairs.answer: Banks shall obtain an undertaking from FPIs or the Global Custodian acting on behalf of the FPI that as and when required, the exempted documents as detailed in Annex IV will be submitted.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of accepting KYC documents from FPIs?
qa_pairs.answer: The purpose of accepting KYC documents from FPIs is for the purpose of investment under Portfolio Investment Scheme (PIS).

qa_pairs.question: What rules govern the acceptance of KYC documents from FPIs?
qa_pairs.answer: The acceptance of KYC documents from FPIs is subject to Income Tax (FATCA/CRS) Rules.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when a customer's business relationship ends?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall preserve the records pertaining to the identification of the customers and their addresses obtained while opening the account and during the course of business relationship, for at least five years after the business relationship is ended.

qa_pairs.question: What is the monetary/time limit for maintaining records of customer transactions?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall maintain all necessary records of transactions between the RE and the customer, both domestic and international, for at least five years from the date of transaction.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the requirement to register customer details on the DARPAN Portal not applicable?
qa_pairs.answer: The requirement to register customer details on the DARPAN Portal is not applicable if the customer is not a non-profit organisation.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a non-profit organisation for the purpose of registering customer details on the DARPAN Portal?
qa_pairs.answer: The section does not explicitly define a non-profit organisation, but it is implied that it refers to organisations that are registered as non-profit under the relevant laws.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for registering customer details on the DARPAN Portal for non-profit organisations?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall register the details of non-profit organisation customers on the DARPAN Portal, and maintain such registration records for a period of five years after the business relationship between the customer and the RE has ended or the account has been closed, whichever is later.

qa_pairs.question: What information must regulated entities maintain in respect of transactions prescribed under PML Rule 3?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall maintain all necessary information in respect of transactions prescribed under PML Rule 3 so as to permit reconstruction of individual transaction, including the nature of the transactions, the amount of the transaction and the currency in which it was denominated, the date on which the transaction was conducted, and the parties to the transaction.

qa_pairs.question: What is the format in which regulated entities must maintain records of customer identity and address?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall maintain records of the identity and address of their customer, and records in respect of transactions referred to in Rule 3 in hard or soft format.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of maintaining records of customer transactions?
qa_pairs.answer: The purpose of maintaining records of customer transactions is to permit reconstruction of individual transaction, including the nature of the transactions, the amount of the transaction and the currency in which it was denominated, the date on which the transaction was conducted, and the parties to the transaction.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when requested by competent authorities?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall make available swiftly, the identification records and transaction data to the competent authorities upon request.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when reporting to the Financial Intelligence Unit-India?
qa_pairs.answer: REs shall furnish to the Director, Financial Intelligence Unit-India (FIU-IND),

qa_pairs.question: What is the threshold for reporting to the Financial Intelligence Unit-India?
qa_pairs.answer: No specific threshold is mentioned in this section.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is reporting to the Financial Intelligence Unit-India not required?
qa_pairs.answer: No specific exception is mentioned in this section.

qa_pairs.question: Who is responsible for furnishing information to the Financial Intelligence Unit-India?
qa_pairs.answer: REs are responsible for furnishing information to the Director, Financial Intelligence Unit-India (FIU-IND).

qa_pairs.question: What is the process for furnishing information to the Financial Intelligence Unit-India?
qa_pairs.answer: The process is not explicitly mentioned in this section, but REs shall furnish to the Director, Financial Intelligence Unit-India (FIU-IND).

qa_pairs.question: What information must REs furnish to the Financial Intelligence Unit-India?
qa_pairs.answer: The specific information to be furnished is not mentioned in this section.

qa_pairs.question: To whom must REs furnish information when reporting to the Financial Intelligence Unit-India?
qa_pairs.answer: REs shall furnish to the Director, Financial Intelligence Unit-India (FIU-IND).

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of furnishing information to the Financial Intelligence Unit-India?
qa_pairs.answer: The purpose of furnishing information is not explicitly mentioned in this section.

qa_pairs.question: What must the Director, FIU-IND do regarding the form of furnishing information?
qa_pairs.answer: The Director, FIU-IND shall direct the REs about the form of furnishing information.

qa_pairs.question: What is the monetary/time limit for issuing guidelines by the Director, FIU-IND?
qa_pairs.answer: No specific monetary/time limit is mentioned in the section.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the Director, FIU-IND not required to specify the procedure and manner of furnishing information?
qa_pairs.answer: No specific conditions are mentioned in the section; however, the Director, FIU-IND is expected to specify the procedure and manner of furnishing information.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a Reporting Entity (RE) for the purpose of this section?
qa_pairs.answer: No specific definition is provided in the section; however, it is mentioned that the Director, FIU-IND shall issue guidelines to the REs.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for furnishing information by the Reporting Entities (REs)?
qa_pairs.answer: The Director, FIU-IND shall specify the procedure and manner of furnishing information.

qa_pairs.question: What information must the Reporting Entities (REs) furnish to the Director, FIU-IND?
qa_pairs.answer: The information referred to in rule 3 of the PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005 in terms of rule 7 thereof.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of the Director, FIU-IND issuing guidelines to the Reporting Entities (REs)?
qa_pairs.answer: The purpose is to direct them about the form of furnishing information and to specify the procedure and the manner of furnishing information.

qa_pairs.question: What is the comprehensive reporting format guide prescribed by the Director, FIU-IND?
qa_pairs.answer: No specific information is provided in the section.

qa_pairs.question: What is the reporting format guide prescribed by the Director, FIU-IND?
qa_pairs.answer: No specific information is provided in the section.

qa_pairs.question: What must reporting entities do when preparing prescribed reports?
qa_pairs.answer: Reporting entities shall take note of the editable electronic utilities released by FIU-IND and Report Generation Utility and Report Validation Utility developed to assist them in the preparation of prescribed reports.

qa_pairs.question: What is the threshold for using the editable electronic utilities of CTR/STR?
qa_pairs.answer: Reporting entities which are yet to install/adopt suitable technological tools for extracting CTR/STR from their live transaction data must make use of the editable electronic utilities placed on FIU-IND's website.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the Principal Officer of a reporting entity not required to have a suitable arrangement to cull out transaction details from branches which are not yet computerized?
qa_pairs.answer: The Principal Officer of a reporting entity is not required to have a suitable arrangement to cull out transaction details from branches which are not yet computerized if all branches of the reporting entity are fully computerized.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a reporting entity for the purpose of this section?
qa_pairs.answer: This section applies to all reporting entities.

qa_pairs.question: What is the process for filing electronic Cash Transaction Reports (CTR) / Suspicious Transaction Reports (STR) using the editable electronic utilities of FIU-IND?
qa_pairs.answer: Reporting entities must use the editable electronic utilities of CTR/STR as have been made available by FIU-IND on its website to file electronic CTR/STR.

qa_pairs.question: What is the penalty for delay in furnishing information to the Director, FIU-IND?
qa_pairs.answer: Delay of each day in furnishing information to the Director, FIU-IND, is subject to a penalty.

qa_pairs.question: What is the website where the editable electronic utilities of CTR/STR are available?
qa_pairs.answer: The editable electronic utilities of CTR/STR are available on FIU-IND's website at http://fiuindia.gov.in.

qa_pairs.question: What is the process for reporting entities to feed transaction details from branches which are not yet computerized into an electronic file?
qa_pairs.answer: The Principal Officers of those REs, whose all branches are not fully computerized, shall have suitable arrangement to cull out the transaction details from branches which are not yet computerized and to feed the data into an electronic file with the help of the editable electronic utilities of CTR/STR.

qa_pairs.question: What is the penalty for delay in furnishing information to the Director, FIU-IND, per day?
qa_pairs.answer: Delay of each day in furnishing information to the Director, FIU-IND, is subject to a penalty.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when reporting a transaction or delay of each day in rectifying a mis-represented transaction?
qa_pairs.answer: Such a situation shall be constituted as a separate violation.

qa_pairs.question: What is the time limit for rectifying a mis-represented transaction?
qa_pairs.answer: The time limit is specified in the Rule.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the confidentiality requirement for records not applicable?
qa_pairs.answer: The confidentiality requirement shall not inhibit sharing of information under paragraph 4(b) of this Master Direction of any analysis of transactions and activities which appear unusual.

qa_pairs.question: Who is responsible for ensuring the maintenance of records referred to in rule 3 of the PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005 and furnishing of the information to the Director?
qa_pairs.answer: Every RE, its directors, officers, and all employees shall ensure this.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of analysis of transactions and activities which appear unusual?
qa_pairs.answer: Such analysis is done to identify unusual transactions and activities.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for sharing information under paragraph 4(b) of this Master Direction?
qa_pairs.answer: The confidentiality requirement shall not inhibit sharing of information under paragraph 4(b) of this Master Direction of any analysis of transactions and activities which appear unusual.

qa_pairs.question: What is the effect of filing a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) on operations in an account?
qa_pairs.answer: REs shall not put any restriction on operations in the accounts merely on the basis of the STR filed.

qa_pairs.question: What is the requirement for confidentiality of records?
qa_pairs.answer: However, such confidentiality requirement shall not inhibit sharing of information under paragraph 4(b) of this Master Direction of any analysis of transactions and activities which appear unusual, if any such analysis has been done.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when transactions are inconsistent with risk categorization and customer profile?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities must put robust software into use as a part of effective identification and reporting of suspicious transactions.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of using robust software in regulated entities?
qa_pairs.answer: The purpose is effective identification and reporting of suspicious transactions.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the use of robust software not required?
qa_pairs.answer: There is no exception mentioned in this section, implying that the use of robust software is mandatory.

qa_pairs.question: What type of transactions trigger the use of robust software?
qa_pairs.answer: Transactions inconsistent with risk categorization and updated customer profile trigger the use of robust software.

qa_pairs.question: What is the process for implementing robust software in regulated entities?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall put robust software into use as a part of effective identification and reporting of suspicious transactions.

qa_pairs.question: What is the expected outcome of using robust software in regulated entities?
qa_pairs.answer: The expected outcome is effective identification and reporting of suspicious transactions.

qa_pairs.question: Is the use of robust software mandatory for regulated entities?
qa_pairs.answer: Yes, the use of robust software is mandatory for regulated entities.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of throwing alerts when transactions are inconsistent with risk categorization and customer profile?
qa_pairs.answer: The purpose is effective identification and reporting of suspicious transactions.

qa_pairs.question: What must banks do when receiving communications from international agencies?
qa_pairs.answer: Banks must report such communications to the Reserve Bank of India as per the requirements under International Agreements.

qa_pairs.question: What is the monetary limit for reporting communications from international agencies?
qa_pairs.answer: There is no specific monetary limit mentioned in the section for reporting communications from international agencies.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is reporting of communications from international agencies not required?
qa_pairs.answer: Reporting of communications from international agencies is not required if they are deemed to be of a routine or non-material nature.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as an international agency for the purpose of this section?
qa_pairs.answer: The Reserve Bank of India will specify the international agencies that are covered under this section.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for reporting communications from international agencies?
qa_pairs.answer: The Reserve Bank of India will specify the procedure for reporting communications from international agencies.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of reporting communications from international agencies?
qa_pairs.answer: The purpose of reporting communications from international agencies is to comply with the requirements under International Agreements.

qa_pairs.question: To whom must banks report communications from international agencies?
qa_pairs.answer: Banks must report communications from international agencies to the Reserve Bank of India.

qa_pairs.question: What are the requirements under International Agreements that banks must comply with?
qa_pairs.answer: The requirements under International Agreements that banks must comply with include reporting communications from international agencies.

qa_pairs.question: What must REs ensure when dealing with accounts of individuals/entities suspected of having terrorist links?
qa_pairs.answer: REs must ensure that they do not have any account in the name of individuals/entities appearing in the lists of individuals and entities suspected of having terrorist links, which are approved by and periodically circulated by the United Nations Security Council (UNSC).

qa_pairs.question: What is the frequency at which REs must verify the UNSC Sanctions Lists?
qa_pairs.answer: The aforementioned lists shall be verified on a daily basis.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is reporting details of accounts resembling individuals/entities in the lists not required?
qa_pairs.answer: Reporting details of accounts resembling individuals/entities in the lists is not required if the accounts do not resemble any of the individuals/entities in the lists.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a RE under section 51 of the UAPA, 1967?
qa_pairs.answer: The section does not explicitly define who qualifies as a RE, but it is implied that it refers to banks and financial institutions.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for freezing assets under section 51A of UAPA, 1967?
qa_pairs.answer: The procedure laid down in the UAPA Order dated February 2, 2021 (Annex II of this Master Direction), shall be strictly followed and meticulous compliance with the Order issued by the Government shall be ensured.

qa_pairs.question: What is the source of the UNSC Sanctions Lists that REs must refer to?
qa_pairs.answer: The UNSC Sanctions Lists are available at www.un.org/securitycouncil/sanctions/1267/aq_sanctions_list and https://www.un.org/securitycouncil/sanctions/1988/materials.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of reporting details of accounts resembling individuals/entities in the lists to FIU-IND and MHA?
qa_pairs.answer: The purpose is to report details of accounts resembling any of the individuals/entities in the lists, apart from advising Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) as required under UAPA notification dated February 2, 2021 (Annex II of this Master Direction).

qa_pairs.question: What is the date of the UAPA notification that requires advising MHA?
qa_pairs.answer: The date of the UAPA notification is February 2, 2021.

qa_pairs.question: What is the list of Nodal Officers for UAPA available on?
qa_pairs.answer: The list of Nodal Officers for UAPA is available on the website of MHA.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when establishing a relation with a customer?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall run a check, on the given parameters, to verify whether individuals and entities in the designated list are holding any funds, financial asset, etc., in the form of bank account, etc. Under section 12A of the WMD Act, 2005.

qa_pairs.question: What is the monetary/time limit for informing the transaction details to the Central Nodal Officer (CNO)?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall immediately inform the transaction details to the CNO. No specific time limit is mentioned, but it is expected to be done without delay.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the obligation to prevent an individual/entity from conducting financial transactions not required?
qa_pairs.answer: The obligation to prevent an individual/entity from conducting financial transactions is not required if there are no reasons to believe beyond doubt that funds or assets held by a customer would fall under the purview of clause (a) or (b) of sub-section (2) of section 12A of the WMD Act, 2005. However, regulated entities shall still run a check, on the given parameters, at the time of establishing a relation with a customer and on a periodic basis to verify whether individuals and entities in the designated list are holding any funds, financial asset, etc., in the form of bank account, etc. Under section 12A of the WMD Act, 2005.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as the Central Nodal Officer (CNO)?
qa_pairs.answer: The Director, FIU-India has been designated as the CNO in terms of Paragraph 1 of the Order. Under section 12A of the WMD Act, 2005.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for unfreezing of funds, etc.?
qa_pairs.answer: The process of unfreezing of funds, etc. shall be observed as per paragraph 7 of the Order. Regulated entities shall forward a copy of application received from an individual/entity regarding unfreezing, along with full details of the asset frozen, as given by the applicant, to the CNO by email, FAX and by post, within two working days. Under section 12A of the WMD Act, 2005.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when an order to freeze assets under section 12A is received from the CNO?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall, without delay, take necessary action to comply with the Order. Under section 12A of the WMD Act, 2005.

qa_pairs.question: What is the designated list that regulated entities may refer to?
qa_pairs.answer: The designated list, as amended from time to time, is available on the portal of FIU-India. Under section 12A of the WMD Act, 2005.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do in case of a match in the designated list?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall immediately inform the transaction details with full particulars of the funds, financial assets or economic resources involved to the Central Nodal Officer (CNO), designated as the authority to exercise powers under section 12A of the WMD Act, 2005. A copy of the communication shall be sent to State Nodal Officer, where the account / transaction is held and to the RBI. Under section 12A of the WMD Act, 2005.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for preventing an individual/entity from conducting financial transactions?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall prevent such individual/entity from conducting financial transactions, under intimation to the CNO by email, FAX and by post, without delay. In case there are reasons to believe beyond doubt that funds or assets held by a customer would fall under the purview of clause (a) or (b) of sub-section (2) of section 12A of the WMD Act, 2005. Under section 12A of the WMD Act, 2005.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when the UNSC 1718 Sanctions List is modified?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall verify the list every day to take into account any modifications, additions, deletions or other changes.

qa_pairs.question: What lists must regulated entities consider for compliance with Government orders?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities must take into account other UNSCRs, lists in the first schedule and the fourth schedule of UAPA, 1967, and any amendments to the same.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is a regulated entity not required to undertake countermeasures?
qa_pairs.answer: A regulated entity is not required to undertake countermeasures unless called upon to do so by any international or intergovernmental organisation of which India is a member and accepted by the Central Government.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a designated individual or entity under the UNSC 1718 Sanctions List?
qa_pairs.answer: The list contains designated individuals and entities, as available at https://www.mea.gov.in/Implementation-n-of-UNSC-Sanctions-DPRK.htm.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for regulated entities to ensure compliance with the Government orders on implementation of section 51A of the UAPA and section 12A of the WMD Act?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities must take into account lists in the first schedule and the fourth schedule of UAPA, 1967, and any amendments to the same for compliance with the Government orders.

qa_pairs.question: What is the frequency of verification of the UNSC 1718 Sanctions List by regulated entities?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall verify the list every day.

qa_pairs.question: What is the source of the UNSC 1718 Sanctions List for regulated entities?
qa_pairs.answer: The list is available at https://www.mea.gov.in/Implementation-n-of-UNSC-Sanctions-DPRK.htm.

qa_pairs.question: What is the role of the Central Government in relation to the UNSC 1718 Sanctions List?
qa_pairs.answer: The Central Government is responsible for accepting any call for countermeasures from international or intergovernmental organisations of which India is a member.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when called upon to undertake countermeasures by an international or intergovernmental organisation?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall undertake countermeasures when called upon to do so by any international or intergovernmental organisation of which India is a member and accepted by the Central Government.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when dealing with countries that do not or insufficiently apply the FATF Recommendations?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall apply enhanced due diligence measures, which are effective and proportionate to the risks, to business relationships and transactions with natural and legal persons (including financial institutions) from countries for which this is called for by the FATF.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of examining the background and purpose of transactions with persons from jurisdictions included in FATF Statements?
qa_pairs.answer: The background and purpose of transactions with persons (including legal persons and other financial institutions) from jurisdictions included in FATF Statements and countries that do not or insufficiently apply the FATF Recommendations shall be examined, and written findings together with all documents shall be retained and shall be made available to Reserve Bank/other relevant authorities, on request.

qa_pairs.question: Who is required to give special attention to business relationships and transactions with persons from or in countries that do not or insufficiently apply the FATF Recommendations?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall give special attention to business relationships and transactions with persons (including legal persons and other financial institutions) from or in countries that do not or insufficiently apply the FATF Recommendations and jurisdictions included in FATF Statements.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of retaining written findings and documents related to transactions with persons from jurisdictions included in FATF Statements?
qa_pairs.answer: The background and purpose of transactions with persons (including legal persons and other financial institutions) from jurisdictions included in FATF Statements and countries that do not or insufficiently apply the FATF Recommendations shall be examined, and written findings together with all documents shall be retained and shall be made available to Reserve Bank/other relevant authorities, on request.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is it not required to preclude legitimate trade and business transactions with countries and jurisdictions mentioned in the FATF statement?
qa_pairs.answer: The processes referred to in (a) & (b) above do not preclude REs from having legitimate trade and business transactions with the countries and jurisdictions mentioned in the FATF statement.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of applying enhanced due diligence measures to business relationships and transactions with natural and legal persons from countries that do not or insufficiently apply the FATF Recommendations?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall apply enhanced due diligence measures, which are effective and proportionate to the risks, to business relationships and transactions with natural and legal persons (including financial institutions) from countries for which this is called for by the FATF.

qa_pairs.question: What is the definition of a country that does not or insufficiently apply the FATF Recommendations?
qa_pairs.answer: Countries that do not or insufficiently apply the FATF Recommendations are identified by FATF Statements circulated by Reserve Bank of India from time to time, and publicly available information.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when examining the background and purpose of transactions with persons from jurisdictions included in FATF Statements?
qa_pairs.answer: The background and purpose of transactions with persons (including legal persons and other financial institutions) from jurisdictions included in FATF Statements and countries that do not or insufficiently apply the FATF Recommendations shall be examined, and written findings together with all documents shall be retained and shall be made available to Reserve Bank/other relevant authorities, on request.
