qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of giving special attention to business relationships and transactions with persons from or in countries that do not or insufficiently apply the FATF Recommendations?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall give special attention to business relationships and transactions with persons (including legal persons and other financial institutions) from or in countries that do not or insufficiently apply the FATF Recommendations and jurisdictions included in FATF Statements.

qa_pairs.question: What must REs do regarding customer information?
qa_pairs.answer: REs shall maintain secrecy regarding the customer information which arises out of the contractual relationship between the RE and customer.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose for which information collected from customers must not be divulged?
qa_pairs.answer: The details thereof shall not be divulged for the purpose of cross selling, or for any other purpose without the express permission of the customer.

qa_pairs.question: What conditions must REs satisfy while considering requests for data/information from Government and other agencies?
qa_pairs.answer: REs shall satisfy themselves that the information being sought is not of such a nature as will violate the provisions of the laws relating to secrecy in the transactions.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the secrecy rule not applicable?
qa_pairs.answer: The exceptions to the said rule shall be as under: i. Where disclosure is under compulsion of law, ii. Where there is a duty to the public to disclose, iii. Where the interest of RE requires disclosure, and iv. Where the disclosure is made with the express or implied consent of the customer.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a customer for the purpose of secrecy obligations?
qa_pairs.answer: Any individual or entity with whom the RE has a contractual relationship.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for considering requests for data/information from Government and other agencies?
qa_pairs.answer: REs shall satisfy themselves that the information being sought is not of such a nature as will violate the provisions of the laws relating to secrecy in the transactions.

qa_pairs.question: What is the monetary/time limit for maintaining secrecy regarding customer information?
qa_pairs.answer: There is no specific monetary/time limit mentioned in the section.

qa_pairs.question: What must banks ensure regarding the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010?
qa_pairs.answer: Banks shall ensure adherence to the provisions of Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010 and Rules made thereunder.

qa_pairs.question: What must REs do when an account-based relationship commences with a customer?
qa_pairs.answer: REs shall capture customer's KYC records and upload onto CKYCR within 10 days of commencement of an account-based relationship with the customer.

qa_pairs.question: What is the monetary/time limit for uploading KYC records onto CKYCR?
qa_pairs.answer: REs shall capture customer's KYC records and upload onto CKYCR within 10 days of commencement of an account-based relationship with the customer.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is a customer not required to submit the same KYC records or information?
qa_pairs.answer: Unless there is a change in the information of the customer as existing in the records of CKYCR, or the KYC record or information retrieved is incomplete or is not as per the current applicable KYC norms, or the validity period of downloaded documents has lapsed, or the RE considers it necessary in order to verify the identity or address (including current address) of the customer, or to perform enhanced due diligence or to build an appropriate risk profile of the customer.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a customer for the purpose of establishing an account-based relationship?
qa_pairs.answer: Individuals and Legal Entities (LEs) qualify as customers for the purpose of establishing an account-based relationship.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for uploading KYC data for new individual accounts opened on or after January 1, 2017?
qa_pairs.answer: Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs) are required to invariably upload the KYC data pertaining to all new individual accounts opened on or after January 1, 2017, with CKYCR. SCBs were initially allowed time up-to February 1, 2017, for uploading data in respect of accounts opened during January 2017.

qa_pairs.question: What must REs do when they obtain additional or updated information from a customer?
qa_pairs.answer: The RE shall within seven days or within such period as may be notified by the Central Government, furnish the updated information to CKYCR, which shall update the KYC records of the existing customer in CKYCR.

qa_pairs.question: What is the time limit for uploading KYC data pertaining to accounts of LEs opened on or after April 1, 2021?
qa_pairs.answer: REs shall upload KYC records pertaining to accounts of LEs opened on or after April 1, 2021, with CKYCR in terms of the provisions of the Rules ibid.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is a customer migrated to the current CDD standard during periodic updation?
qa_pairs.answer: REs shall ensure that during periodic updation, the customers are migrated to the current CDD standard.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for retrieving updated KYC records from CKYCR after an update in the KYC record of an existing customer?
qa_pairs.answer: Once CKYCR informs an RE regarding an update in the KYC record of an existing customer, the RE shall retrieve the updated KYC records from CKYCR and update the KYC record maintained by the RE.

qa_pairs.question: What must Reporting Entities do when determining whether they are a Reporting Financial Institution?
qa_pairs.answer: Reporting Entities shall determine whether they are a Reporting Financial Institution as defined in Income Tax Rule 114F and if so, shall take the following steps for complying with the reporting requirements.

qa_pairs.question: What is the link for registering on the related e-filling portal of Income Tax Department as Reporting Financial Institutions?
qa_pairs.answer: The link for registering on the related e-filling portal of Income Tax Department as Reporting Financial Institutions is https://incometaxindiaefiling.gov.in/ post login -> My Account --> Register as Reporting Financial Institution.

qa_pairs.question: Who is permitted to use the digital signature for submitting online reports?
qa_pairs.answer: The ‘Designated Director’ is permitted to use the digital signature for submitting online reports.

qa_pairs.question: What must Reporting Entities refer to for carrying out the due diligence procedure for identifying reportable accounts?
qa_pairs.answer: Reporting Entities shall refer to the spot reference rates published by Foreign Exchange Dealers’ Association of India (FEDAI) on their website at http://www.fedai.org.in/RevaluationRates.aspx for carrying out the due diligence procedure for the purposes of identifying reportable accounts in terms of Rule 114H.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of developing an Information Technology (IT) framework for Reporting Entities?
qa_pairs.answer: The purpose of developing an Information Technology (IT) framework for Reporting Entities is for carrying out due diligence procedure and for recording and maintaining the same, as provided in Rule 114H.

qa_pairs.question: What is the responsibility of the High Level Monitoring Committee constituted by Reporting Entities?
qa_pairs.answer: The High Level Monitoring Committee constituted by Reporting Entities is responsible to ensure compliance with the reporting requirements.

qa_pairs.question: What must Reporting Entities do to ensure compliance with updated instructions/rules/guidance notes/Press releases issued by Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT)?
qa_pairs.answer: Reporting Entities must ensure compliance with updated instructions/rules/guidance notes/Press releases issued by Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) from time to time and available on the web site http://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/Pages/default.aspx.

qa_pairs.question: What are the sources of updated information that Reporting Entities may take note of?
qa_pairs.answer: Reporting Entities may take note of the following sources of updated information: i. updated Guidance Note on FATCA and CRS ii. a press release on ‘Closure of Financial Accounts’ under Rule 114H (8).

qa_pairs.question: What is the maximum period for presenting payment instruments?
qa_pairs.answer: Three months from the date of such instruments.

qa_pairs.question: What must banks do when a cheque/draft/pay order/banker's cheque is presented beyond the specified period?
qa_pairs.answer: They shall not make payment.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is a bank permitted to make payment on a cheque/draft/pay order/banker's cheque presented beyond the specified period?
qa_pairs.answer: None, as payment shall not be made.

qa_pairs.question: What is the period after which a cheque/draft/pay order/banker's cheque is considered stale?
qa_pairs.answer: Three months from the date of such instruments.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for determining whether a cheque/draft/pay order/banker's cheque is eligible for payment?
qa_pairs.answer: Banks must check the date of the instrument and ensure it is within the specified period.

qa_pairs.question: What happens to a cheque/draft/pay order/banker's cheque that is presented beyond the specified period?
qa_pairs.answer: Payment shall not be made.

qa_pairs.question: Is a bank required to make payment on a cheque/draft/pay order/banker's cheque presented within the specified period?
qa_pairs.answer: Yes, payment must be made.

qa_pairs.question: What is the date from which the three-month period for presenting payment instruments is calculated?
qa_pairs.answer: The date of such instruments.

qa_pairs.question: What must banks do to minimize the operations of Money Mules?
qa_pairs.answer: Banks shall undertake diligence measures and meticulous monitoring to identify accounts which are operated as Money Mules and take appropriate action.

qa_pairs.question: What is the consequence if a bank fails to file an STR for a Money Mule account?
qa_pairs.answer: It shall then be deemed that the bank has not complied with these directions.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of monitoring transactions as per these directions?
qa_pairs.answer: The purpose is to minimise the operations of “Money Mules” which are used to launder the proceeds of fraud schemes.

qa_pairs.question: What action must banks take if an account is identified as a Money Mule?
qa_pairs.answer: Banks must take appropriate action, including reporting of suspicious transactions to FIU-IND.

qa_pairs.question: What is the consequence of not complying with these directions?
qa_pairs.answer: It shall be deemed that the bank has not complied with these directions.

qa_pairs.question: What is the threshold for identifying a Money Mule account?
qa_pairs.answer: There is no specific threshold mentioned in the section.

qa_pairs.question: What diligence measures must banks undertake to identify Money Mule accounts?
qa_pairs.answer: Banks shall undertake diligence measures and meticulous monitoring.

qa_pairs.question: What is the process for identifying and reporting Money Mule accounts?
qa_pairs.answer: Banks shall undertake diligence measures and meticulous monitoring to identify accounts which are operated as Money Mules and take appropriate action, including reporting of suspicious transactions to FIU-IND.

qa_pairs.question: What must banks do when collecting account payee cheques?
qa_pairs.answer: Banks shall collect account payee cheques drawn for an amount not exceeding rupees fifty thousand to the account of their customers who are co-operative credit societies, provided the payees of such cheques are the constituents of such co-operative credit societies.

qa_pairs.question: What is the monetary limit for collecting account payee cheques?
qa_pairs.answer: Rupees fifty thousand

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions can banks collect account payee cheques?
qa_pairs.answer: Banks can collect account payee cheques drawn for an amount not exceeding rupees fifty thousand to the account of their customers who are co-operative credit societies, provided the payees of such cheques are the constituents of such co-operative credit societies.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a constituent of a co-operative credit society for account payee cheque collection?
qa_pairs.answer: The payees of such cheques are the constituents of such co-operative credit societies.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for collecting account payee cheques for co-operative credit societies?
qa_pairs.answer: Banks shall, at their option, collect account payee cheques drawn for an amount not exceeding rupees fifty thousand to the account of their customers who are co-operative credit societies, provided the payees of such cheques are the constituents of such co-operative credit societies.

qa_pairs.question: Can banks collect account payee cheques for any person other than the payee constituent?
qa_pairs.answer: No, account payee cheques for any person other than the payee constituent shall not be collected.

qa_pairs.question: What type of customers can banks collect account payee cheques for?
qa_pairs.answer: Banks can collect account payee cheques for their customers who are co-operative credit societies.

qa_pairs.question: Is there a specific type of account payee cheque that banks can collect?
qa_pairs.answer: Yes, banks can collect account payee cheques drawn for an amount not exceeding rupees fifty thousand.

qa_pairs.question: What must REs do when entering into new relationships with individual customers?
qa_pairs.answer: A Unique Customer Identification Code (UCIC) shall be allotted.

qa_pairs.question: What is the option available to REs when issuing UCIC to walk-in/occasional customers?
qa_pairs.answer: The REs shall, at their option, not issue UCIC to all walk-in/occasional customers.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions can REs not issue UCIC to walk-in/occasional customers?
qa_pairs.answer: Provided it is ensured that there is adequate mechanism to identify such walk-in customers who have frequent transactions with them.

qa_pairs.question: Who is required to be allotted a UCIC by REs?
qa_pairs.answer: Individual customers, both new and existing.

qa_pairs.question: What is the process for allotting UCIC to individual customers?
qa_pairs.answer: The REs shall allot UCIC while entering into new relationships with individual customers as also the existing individual customers.

qa_pairs.question: What type of customers are exempt from being allotted a UCIC by REs?
qa_pairs.answer: Walk-in/occasional customers, provided the conditions are met.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of allotting UCIC to individual customers by REs?
qa_pairs.answer: To uniquely identify customers.

qa_pairs.question: What is the threshold for frequent transactions with walk-in customers to be allotted a UCIC?
qa_pairs.answer: Not specified.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when developing new products and business practices?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall identify and assess the ML/TF risks that may arise in relation to the development of new products and new business practices, including new delivery mechanisms, and the use of new or developing technologies for both new and pre-existing products.

qa_pairs.question: What is the time limit for undertaking ML/TF risk assessments prior to the launch or use of new products, practices, services, and technologies?
qa_pairs.answer: There is no specific time limit mentioned in the section, but it is implied that the risk assessments must be undertaken prior to the launch or use of such products, practices, services, and technologies.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is a risk-based approach not required for managing and mitigating ML/TF risks?
qa_pairs.answer: There is no exception mentioned in the section, implying that a risk-based approach is always required for managing and mitigating ML/TF risks.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a regulated entity for the purpose of this section?
qa_pairs.answer: The section does not explicitly define who qualifies as a regulated entity, but it is implied that it refers to entities that are subject to the RBI's AML/CFT regulations.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for adopting a risk-based approach to manage and mitigate ML/TF risks?
qa_pairs.answer: The section does not provide a detailed procedure, but it mentions that regulated entities shall adopt a risk-based approach through appropriate EDD measures and transaction monitoring, etc.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do to manage and mitigate ML/TF risks through EDD measures and transaction monitoring?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall adopt a risk-based approach to manage and mitigate the risks through appropriate EDD measures and transaction monitoring, etc.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of undertaking ML/TF risk assessments prior to the launch or use of new products, practices, services, and technologies?
qa_pairs.answer: The purpose is to identify and assess the ML/TF risks that may arise in relation to the development of new products and new business practices, including new delivery mechanisms, and the use of new or developing technologies for both new and pre-existing products.

qa_pairs.question: What are the EDD measures and transaction monitoring that regulated entities are expected to adopt?
qa_pairs.answer: The section does not provide a detailed list, but it mentions that regulated entities shall adopt appropriate EDD measures and transaction monitoring, etc.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do to ensure that they are managing and mitigating ML/TF risks effectively?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall ensure that they undertake the ML/TF risk assessments prior to the launch or use of such products, practices, services, technologies, and adopt a risk-based approach to manage and mitigate the risks through appropriate EDD measures and transaction monitoring, etc.

qa_pairs.question: What must banks do when establishing a new correspondent banking relationship?
qa_pairs.answer: Banks must obtain prior approval from senior management and post facto approval from the Board or the Committee empowered for this purpose.

qa_pairs.question: What is the minimum information that banks must gather about a respondent bank?
qa_pairs.answer: Banks must gather sufficient information about a respondent bank to understand fully the nature of the respondent bank’s business and to determine from publicly available information the reputation of the respondent bank and the quality of supervision.

qa_pairs.question: What is the condition under which a correspondent bank is not required to enter into or continue a correspondent relationship?
qa_pairs.answer: A correspondent relationship shall not be entered into or continued with a shell bank.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a shell bank for the purpose of correspondent banking?
qa_pairs.answer: A shell bank is not explicitly defined in this section, but it is implied that a shell bank is a bank that lacks a physical presence or a meaningful business activity.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for ensuring that respondent banks have conducted CDD on customers having direct access to the accounts of the correspondent bank?
qa_pairs.answer: The correspondent bank shall be satisfied that the respondent bank has conducted CDD on the customers having direct access to the accounts of the correspondent bank and is undertaking on-going 'due diligence' on them.

qa_pairs.question: What is the condition under which a bank is not required to be cautious of correspondent banking relationships with institutions located in jurisdictions which have strategic deficiencies or have not made sufficient progress in implementation of FATF Recommendations?
qa_pairs.answer: This section does not specify any exceptions, but it is implied that banks must always be cautious of correspondent banking relationships with institutions located in such jurisdictions.

qa_pairs.question: What is the minimum time frame within which a respondent bank must be able to provide the relevant CDD information to the correspondent bank?
qa_pairs.answer: The correspondent bank shall ensure that the respondent bank is able to provide the relevant CDD information immediately on request.

qa_pairs.question: What is the condition under which a bank is required to apply enhanced 'due diligence' procedures for transactions carried out through the correspondent accounts?
qa_pairs.answer: Banks shall ensure that respondent banks have KYC/AML policies and procedures in place and apply enhanced 'due diligence' procedures for transactions carried out through the correspondent accounts.

qa_pairs.question: What is the information that banks must include when gathering information about the nature of business of the respondent bank?
qa_pairs.answer: The information gathered in relation to the nature of business of the respondent bank shall include information on management, major business activities, purpose of opening the account, identity of any third-party entities that will use the correspondent banking services, regulatory/supervisory framework in the respondent bank’s home country among other relevant information.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when there is involvement of any unregulated entities in the process of wire transfer?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall be fully responsible for information, reporting and other requirements and therefore shall ensure, inter alia, that, there is unhindered flow of complete wire transfer information, as mandated under these directions, from and through the unregulated entities involved; the agreement / arrangement, if any, with such unregulated entities by REs clearly stipulates the obligations under wire transfer instructions; and a termination clause is available in their agreement / arrangement, if any, with such entities so that in case the unregulated entities are unable to support the wire information requirements, the agreement / arrangement can be terminated.

qa_pairs.question: What is the monetary limit for domestic wire transfers where the originator is not an account holder of the ordering RE?
qa_pairs.answer: Rupees fifty thousand

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the requirement for originator information exempted for individual cross-border wire transfers in a batch file?
qa_pairs.answer: Provided that they include the originator’s account number or unique transaction reference number, and the batch file contains required and accurate originator information, and full beneficiary information, that is fully traceable within the beneficiary country.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a designated person or entity for cross-border transactions?
qa_pairs.answer: As per Chapter IX of the Master Direction, REs shall ensure that they do not process cross-border transactions of designated persons and entities.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for retaining originator and beneficiary information accompanying a wire transfer by an intermediary RE?
qa_pairs.answer: The intermediary RE shall retain the information with the transfer, and where technical limitations prevent this, the intermediary RE shall keep a record, for at least five years, of all the information received from the ordering financial institution or another intermediary RE.

qa_pairs.question: What must the ordering RE do if a customer, who is not an account holder of the ordering RE, is intentionally structuring domestic wire transfers below rupees fifty thousand to avoid reporting or monitoring?
qa_pairs.answer: Customer Identification shall be made, and in case of non-cooperation from the customer, efforts shall be made to establish identity and if the same transaction is found to be suspicious, STR may be filed with FIU-IND in accordance with the PML Rules.

qa_pairs.question: What is the time limit for making information available to the beneficiary RE or appropriate authorities by the ordering RE?
qa_pairs.answer: Within three working/business days of receiving the request.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is a unique transaction reference number sufficient for domestic wire transfers below rupees fifty thousand where the originator is not an account holder of the ordering RE?
qa_pairs.answer: Provided that this number or identifier will permit the transaction to be traced back to the originator or the beneficiary.

qa_pairs.question: What must the beneficiary RE do to identify cross-border wire transfers and qualifying domestic wire transfers that lack required originator information or required beneficiary information?
qa_pairs.answer: Beneficiary RE shall take reasonable measures, including post-event monitoring or real-time monitoring where feasible, to identify such wire transfers.

qa_pairs.question: What is the monetary limit for issuing demand drafts, etc., against cash payment?
qa_pairs.answer: Rupees fifty thousand and above

qa_pairs.question: What must the issuing bank do for demand drafts, pay orders, banker's cheques, etc., issued on or after September 15, 2018?
qa_pairs.answer: Incorporate the name of the purchaser on the face of the instrument

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the name of the purchaser not required to be incorporated on the face of the demand draft, pay order, banker's cheque, etc.?
qa_pairs.answer: The instructions do not specify any exceptions, implying that the name of the purchaser must be incorporated in all cases

qa_pairs.question: What modes of remittance of funds are permitted for values of rupees fifty thousand and above?
qa_pairs.answer: Demand draft, mail/telegraphic transfer, NEFT, IMPS, or any other mode

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for issuing demand drafts, etc., for values of rupees fifty thousand and above?
qa_pairs.answer: The instrument shall be issued by debit to the customer's account or against cheques

qa_pairs.question: What is the effective date for the instructions regarding the issue and payment of demand drafts, etc.?
qa_pairs.answer: September 15, 2018

qa_pairs.question: What must the issuing bank not do for demand drafts, pay orders, banker's cheques, etc., issued on or after September 15, 2018?
qa_pairs.answer: Issue the instrument without incorporating the name of the purchaser on the face of the instrument

qa_pairs.question: What is the minimum value for which demand drafts, etc., must be issued by debit to the customer's account or against cheques?
qa_pairs.answer: Rupees fifty thousand

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when undertaking transactions?
qa_pairs.answer: They shall obtain and verify the Permanent account number (PAN) or equivalent e-document thereof of customers.

qa_pairs.question: What is the equivalent e-document of PAN that can be obtained from customers?
qa_pairs.answer: The equivalent e-document of PAN is not specified in the section, but it is expected to be as per the provisions of Income Tax Rule 114B applicable to banks, as amended from time to time.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is obtaining a PAN not required?
qa_pairs.answer: Obtaining a PAN is not required from persons who do not have PAN or equivalent e-document thereof, in which case Form 60 shall be obtained.

qa_pairs.question: What form must be obtained from persons who do not have PAN or equivalent e-document?
qa_pairs.answer: Form 60 must be obtained from persons who do not have PAN or equivalent e-document thereof.

qa_pairs.question: What rule governs the provisions for obtaining PAN from customers?
qa_pairs.answer: The provisions for obtaining PAN from customers are governed by Income Tax Rule 114B applicable to banks, as amended from time to time.

qa_pairs.question: What is the process for obtaining Form 60 from customers who do not have PAN?
qa_pairs.answer: The process for obtaining Form 60 from customers who do not have PAN or equivalent e-document thereof is not specified in the section.

qa_pairs.question: What is the threshold for requiring PAN from customers?
qa_pairs.answer: There is no specific threshold mentioned in the section for requiring PAN from customers.

qa_pairs.question: What must be verified along with PAN or equivalent e-document?
qa_pairs.answer: The Permanent account number (PAN) or equivalent e-document thereof of customers must be verified while undertaking transactions.

qa_pairs.question: What must REs do when selling third-party products?
qa_pairs.answer: REs acting as agents shall comply with the following aspects: the identity and address of the walk-in customer shall be verified for transactions above rupees fifty thousand as required under paragraph 13(e) of this Direction.

qa_pairs.question: What is the monetary limit for verifying the identity and address of the walk-in customer?
qa_pairs.answer: Transactions above rupees fifty thousand require verification of the identity and address of the walk-in customer.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the obligation to verify the identity and address of the walk-in customer not required?
qa_pairs.answer: The obligation to verify the identity and address of the walk-in customer is not required for transactions below rupees fifty thousand.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a walk-in customer for the purpose of these directions?
qa_pairs.answer: The Direction does not explicitly define a walk-in customer, but it is implied that a walk-in customer is a customer who is not an account-based customer.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for maintaining transaction details of sale of third-party products and related records?
qa_pairs.answer: Transaction details of sale of third-party products and related records shall be maintained as prescribed in paragraph 46 of Chapter VII.

qa_pairs.question: What AML software capabilities are required for the purpose of filing CTR/STR in respect of transactions relating to third-party products?
qa_pairs.answer: AML software capable of capturing, generating and analysing alerts for the purpose of filing CTR/STR in respect of transactions relating to third-party products with customers including walk-in customers shall be available.

qa_pairs.question: What are the permitted methods for undertaking transactions involving rupees fifty thousand and above?
qa_pairs.answer: Transactions involving rupees fifty thousand and above shall be undertaken only by debit to customers’ account or against cheques; and obtaining and verifying the PAN given by the account-based as well as walk-in customers.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the instruction at paragraph d above also applicable to sale of REs’ own products?
qa_pairs.answer: The instruction at paragraph d above shall also apply to sale of REs’ own products, payment of dues of credit cards/sale and reloading of prepaid/travel cards and any other product for rupees fifty thousand and above.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of filing CTR/STR in respect of transactions relating to third-party products?
qa_pairs.answer: The purpose of filing CTR/STR in respect of transactions relating to third-party products is to capture, generate and analyse alerts for AML purposes.

qa_pairs.question: What must commercial banks do regarding the 'at par' cheque facility offered to co-operative banks?
qa_pairs.answer: The 'at par' cheque facility offered by commercial banks to co-operative banks shall be monitored and such arrangements be reviewed to assess the risks including credit risk and reputational risk arising therefrom.

qa_pairs.question: What is the monetary limit for transactions by account-holders of co-operative banks who are KYC compliant?
qa_pairs.answer: Rupees fifty thousand or more

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the 'at par' cheque facility not permitted to be utilised by co-operative banks?
qa_pairs.answer: The facility is not permitted to be utilised for transactions exceeding rupees fifty thousand or for non-KYC compliant account-holders, and also not permitted to be utilised for transactions exceeding rupees fifty thousand for walk-in customers against cash.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a KYC compliant account-holder for the purpose of availing the 'at par' cheque facility?
qa_pairs.answer: An account-holder who is KYC compliant, provided that all transactions of rupees fifty thousand or more are strictly by debit to the customers' accounts.

qa_pairs.question: What records must co-operative banks maintain regarding the issuance of 'at par' cheques?
qa_pairs.answer: Records pertaining to issuance of 'at par' cheques covering, inter alia, applicant's name and account number, beneficiary's details and date of issuance of the 'at par' cheque.

qa_pairs.question: What is the requirement for 'At par' cheques issued by co-operative banks?
qa_pairs.answer: The 'At par' cheques issued are crossed 'account payee' irrespective of the amount involved.

qa_pairs.question: What is the requirement for sufficient balances/drawing arrangements with the commercial bank extending the 'at par' cheque facility?
qa_pairs.answer: Co-operative banks must maintain sufficient balances/drawing arrangements with the commercial bank extending such facility for purpose of honouring such instruments.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of honouring 'at par' cheques by commercial banks extending the facility to co-operative banks?
qa_pairs.answer: The purpose of honouring such instruments is to ensure that the 'at par' cheques issued by co-operative banks are honoured by the commercial bank extending the facility.

qa_pairs.question: What is the condition for honouring 'at par' cheques for walk-in customers against cash?
qa_pairs.answer: The condition is that the amount involved is less than rupees fifty thousand per individual.

qa_pairs.question: What must PPI issuers do regarding Master Direction instructions?
qa_pairs.answer: PPI issuers shall ensure that the instructions issued by Department of Payment and Settlement System of Reserve Bank of India through their Master Direction are strictly adhered to.

qa_pairs.question: What is the threshold for PPI issuers to adhere to Master Direction instructions?
qa_pairs.answer: There is no specific monetary or time limit mentioned in the section for PPI issuers to adhere to Master Direction instructions.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is a PPI issuer not required to adhere to Master Direction instructions?
qa_pairs.answer: There is no exception mentioned in the section for PPI issuers not to adhere to Master Direction instructions. PPI issuers are strictly required to adhere to the instructions.

qa_pairs.question: Who issues instructions for PPI issuers to follow?
qa_pairs.answer: The Department of Payment and Settlement System of Reserve Bank of India issues instructions for PPI issuers to follow through their Master Direction.

qa_pairs.question: What is the process for PPI issuers to ensure adherence to Master Direction instructions?
qa_pairs.answer: PPI issuers must ensure that the instructions issued by Department of Payment and Settlement System of Reserve Bank of India through their Master Direction are strictly adhered to.

qa_pairs.question: What is the consequence of a PPI issuer not adhering to Master Direction instructions?
qa_pairs.answer: The section does not specify the consequence of a PPI issuer not adhering to Master Direction instructions. However, it is expected that non-adherence may attract regulatory action.

qa_pairs.question: Is a PPI issuer permitted to deviate from Master Direction instructions?
qa_pairs.answer: No, a PPI issuer is not permitted to deviate from Master Direction instructions as they are strictly required to adhere to the instructions.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of Master Direction instructions for PPI issuers?
qa_pairs.answer: The purpose of Master Direction instructions for PPI issuers is to ensure that they strictly adhere to the instructions issued by Department of Payment and Settlement System of Reserve Bank of India.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when hiring employees?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities shall put in place an adequate screening mechanism, including Know Your Employee / Staff policy, as an integral part of their personnel recruitment/hiring process.

qa_pairs.question: What skills must staff dealing with KYC/AML/CFT matters possess?
qa_pairs.answer: Staff dealing with KYC/AML/CFT matters must have high integrity and ethical standards, good understanding of extant KYC/AML/CFT standards, effective communication skills and ability to keep up with the changing KYC/AML/CFT landscape, nationally and internationally.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the on-going employee training programme not required?
qa_pairs.answer: There is no specific condition mentioned in this section for exemption from the on-going employee training programme. However, the section does not explicitly state that it is mandatory for all staff, implying that it may not be required for certain roles or staff categories.

qa_pairs.question: What is the focus of the training for frontline staff?
qa_pairs.answer: The focus of the training for frontline staff shall be to handle issues arising from lack of customer education.

qa_pairs.question: What must be ensured for the audit function?
qa_pairs.answer: Proper staffing of the audit function with persons adequately trained and well-versed in KYC/AML/CFT policies of the RE, regulation and related issues shall be ensured.

qa_pairs.question: What is the training requirement for compliance staff?
qa_pairs.answer: Compliance staff shall be adequately trained in KYC/AML/CFT policy.

qa_pairs.question: What is the training requirement for staff dealing with new customers?
qa_pairs.answer: Staff dealing with new customers shall be adequately trained in KYC/AML/CFT policy.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for putting in place an on-going employee training programme?
qa_pairs.answer: The procedure for putting in place an on-going employee training programme is not explicitly stated in this section. However, it is mentioned that the focus of the training shall be different for frontline staff, compliance staff and staff dealing with new customers.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when the new RBI directions are issued?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities must repeal the instructions/guidelines contained in the previous directions with the issue of these directions.

qa_pairs.question: What is the threshold for the applicability of the repeal provisions?
qa_pairs.answer: There is no specific monetary or time limit mentioned for the applicability of the repeal provisions.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the repeal of previous directions not required?
qa_pairs.answer: The repeal of previous directions is not required if the new RBI directions do not supersede the existing instructions/guidelines.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a regulated entity under the repeal provisions?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities include banks, financial institutions, and other entities governed by RBI directions.

qa_pairs.question: What is the process for repealing the instructions/guidelines contained in the previous directions?
qa_pairs.answer: The process for repeal involves issuing new RBI directions that supersede the existing instructions/guidelines.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do with the instructions/guidelines contained in the previous directions after the new RBI directions are issued?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities must repeal the instructions/guidelines contained in the previous directions.

qa_pairs.question: Is there a specific timeline for the repeal of previous directions?
qa_pairs.answer: There is no specific timeline mentioned for the repeal of previous directions.

qa_pairs.question: What is the effect of the new RBI directions on the existing instructions/guidelines?
qa_pairs.answer: The new RBI directions supersede the existing instructions/guidelines.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do with approvals given under repealed circulars?
qa_pairs.answer: These approvals shall be deemed as given under these directions.

qa_pairs.question: What is the effect of the repeal of circulars under these directions?
qa_pairs.answer: All the repealed circulars are deemed to have been in force prior to the coming into force of these directions.

qa_pairs.question: What is the status of approvals given under repealed circulars?
qa_pairs.answer: These approvals shall be deemed as given under these directions.

qa_pairs.question: What is the effect of the coming into force of these directions on repealed circulars?
qa_pairs.answer: All the repealed circulars are deemed to have been in force prior to the coming into force of these directions.

qa_pairs.question: What is the threshold for the application of these directions to repealed circulars?
qa_pairs.answer: There is no specific threshold mentioned in the section.

qa_pairs.question: What is the status of approvals given under repealed circulars prior to the coming into force of these directions?
qa_pairs.answer: These approvals shall be deemed as given under these directions.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions are repealed circulars deemed to have been in force?
qa_pairs.answer: Prior to the coming into force of these directions.

qa_pairs.question: What is the effect of the repeal of circulars on approvals given under them?
qa_pairs.answer: These approvals shall be deemed as given under these directions.

qa_pairs.question: What must the RE do when developing a digital KYC process?
qa_pairs.answer: The RE shall develop an application for digital KYC process which shall be made available at customer touch points for undertaking KYC of their customers and the KYC process shall be undertaken only through this authenticated application of the REs.

qa_pairs.question: What is the monetary/time limit for using the services of Business Correspondent (BC) for the digital KYC process?
qa_pairs.answer: There is no specific monetary/time limit mentioned in the section for using the services of Business Correspondent (BC) for the digital KYC process.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the use of mobile number of authorized officer for customer signature not required?
qa_pairs.answer: The mobile number of authorized officer shall not be used for customer signature. However, in case the customer does not have his/her own mobile number, then mobile number of his/her family/relatives/known persons may be used for this purpose and be clearly mentioned in CAF.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as an authorized officer for the purpose of digital KYC process?
qa_pairs.answer: The authorized officer is the official of the RE who is authorized to undertake the KYC process and verify the customer's details.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for capturing the live photograph of the customer and original documents?
qa_pairs.answer: The live photograph of the customer and original documents shall be captured in proper light so that they are clearly readable and identifiable. The background behind the customer while capturing live photograph should be of white colour and no other person shall come into the frame while capturing the live photograph of the customer.

qa_pairs.question: What must the authorized officer do after verifying the customer's details?
qa_pairs.answer: The authorized officer shall provide a declaration about the capturing of the live photograph of customer and the original document. For this purpose, the authorized official shall be verified with One Time Password (OTP) which will be sent to his mobile number registered with the RE.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of water-marking in the captured live photograph of the customer?
qa_pairs.answer: The system Application of the RE shall put a water-mark in readable form having CAF number, GPS coordinates, authorized official’s name, unique employee Code (assigned by REs) and Date (DD:MM:YYYY) and time stamp (HH:MM:SS) on the captured live photograph of the customer.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for auto-populating the details in the CAF?
qa_pairs.answer: In those documents where Quick Response (QR) code is available, such details can be auto-populated by scanning the QR code instead of manual filing the details.

qa_pairs.question: What must the authorized officer check and verify after the completion of the digital KYC process?
qa_pairs.answer: The authorized officer shall check and verify that: (i) information available in the picture of document is matching with the information entered by authorized officer in CAF. (ii) live photograph of the customer matches with the photo available in the document.; and (iii) all of the necessary details in CAF including mandatory field are filled properly.

qa_pairs.question: What must the Central Government do for the prevention of terrorist activities?
qa_pairs.answer: The Central Government shall have power to freeze, seize or attach funds and other financial assets or economic resources held by, on behalf of or at the direction of the individuals or entities listed in the Schedule to the Order, or any other person engaged in or suspected to be engaged in terrorism.

qa_pairs.question: What is the definition of 'Order' under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967?
qa_pairs.answer: The 'Order' means the Prevention and Suppression of Terrorism (Implementation of Security Council Resolutions) Order, 2007, as may be amended from time to time.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the entry into or transit through India of individuals not prohibited?
qa_pairs.answer: The entry into or transit through India of individuals listed in the Schedule to the Order or any other person engaged in or suspected to be engaged in terrorism is prohibited. However, this does not apply to individuals who are not engaged in or suspected to be engaged in terrorism.

qa_pairs.question: What services are prohibited from being made available for the benefit of individuals or entities listed in the Schedule to the Order?
qa_pairs.answer: Funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services are prohibited from being made available for the benefit of the individuals or entities listed in the Schedule to the Order or any other person engaged in or suspected to be engaged in terrorism.

qa_pairs.question: What is the scope of the Central Government's power to freeze, seize or attach funds and other financial assets or economic resources?
qa_pairs.answer: The Central Government's power to freeze, seize or attach funds and other financial assets or economic resources extends to individuals or entities listed in the Schedule to the Order, or any other person engaged in or suspected to be engaged in terrorism.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for implementing the Central Government's power to freeze, seize or attach funds and other financial assets or economic resources?
qa_pairs.answer: The procedure for implementing the Central Government's power is not specified in this section.

qa_pairs.question: What is the effect of the Central Government's power to prohibit individuals or entities from making funds, financial assets or economic resources available?
qa_pairs.answer: The effect of the Central Government's power is to prohibit any individual or entity from making funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services available for the benefit of the individuals or entities listed in the Schedule to the Order or any other person engaged in or suspected to be engaged in terrorism.

qa_pairs.question: What is the definition of 'Schedule to the Order' under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967?
qa_pairs.answer: The 'Schedule to the Order' refers to the list of individuals or entities listed in the Prevention and Suppression of Terrorism (Implementation of Security Council Resolutions) Order, 2007, as may be amended from time to time.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of the Central Government's power to prevent the entry into or transit through India of individuals listed in the Schedule to the Order?
qa_pairs.answer: The purpose of the Central Government's power is to prevent the entry into or transit through India of individuals listed in the Schedule to the Order or any other person engaged in or suspected to be engaged in terrorism.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do in order to implement the provisions of Section 51A?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities must ensure expeditious and effective implementation of the provisions of Section 51A.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of the revised procedure outlined in Section 2. I?
qa_pairs.answer: The purpose of the revised procedure is to ensure expeditious and effective implementation of the provisions of Section 51A.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the earlier procedure on the subject superseded?
qa_pairs.answer: The earlier procedure on the subject is superseded by the revised procedure outlined in Section 2. I.

qa_pairs.question: What is the subject matter of the revised procedure outlined in Section 2. I?
qa_pairs.answer: The subject matter of the revised procedure is the implementation of the provisions of Section 51A.

qa_pairs.question: What is the effect of the revised procedure on earlier orders and guidelines?
qa_pairs.answer: The revised procedure is in supersession of earlier orders and guidelines on the subject.

qa_pairs.question: Is the revised procedure mandatory for regulated entities?
qa_pairs.answer: Yes, the revised procedure is mandatory for regulated entities to ensure expeditious and effective implementation of the provisions of Section 51A.

qa_pairs.question: What is the scope of the revised procedure outlined in Section 2. I?
qa_pairs.answer: The scope of the revised procedure is the implementation of the provisions of Section 51A.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for implementing the provisions of Section 51A?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities must ensure expeditious and effective implementation of the provisions of Section 51A, as outlined in the revised procedure.

qa_pairs.question: What must the Ministry of External Affairs, Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Foreigners Division of MHA, FIU-IND, Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) and Financial Regulators (RBI, SEBI and IRDA) do?
qa_pairs.answer: They shall appoint a UAPA Nodal Officer and communicate the name and contact details to the Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA.

qa_pairs.question: What is the rank of the UAPA Nodal Officer that States and UTs shall appoint preferably?
qa_pairs.answer: The rank of the Principal Secretary/Secretary, Home Department.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the list of UAPA Nodal Officers not required to be forwarded to all other UAPA Nodal Officers?
qa_pairs.answer: The list is not required to be forwarded when it is not updated.

qa_pairs.question: What is the frequency at which the Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA shall forward the list of UAPA Nodal Officers?
qa_pairs.answer: The list shall be forwarded in July every year or as and when the list is updated.

qa_pairs.question: Who shall forward the consolidated list of UAPA Nodal Officers to the banks, stock exchanges/depositories, intermediaries regulated by SEBI and insurance companies?
qa_pairs.answer: The Financial Regulators shall forward the list.

qa_pairs.question: What is the name and contact details of the Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA?
qa_pairs.answer: The Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA is the Joint Secretary (CTCR), Ministry of Home Affairs with telephone numbers 011-23093124 and 011-230923465 (Fax) and email address jsctcr-mha@gov.in.

qa_pairs.question: What must the Regulators of the real estate agents, dealers in precious metals & stones (DPMS) and DNFBPs do?
qa_pairs.answer: They shall forward the consolidated list of UAPA Nodal Officers to the real estate agents, dealers in precious metals & stones (DPMS) and DNFBPs.

qa_pairs.question: What is the frequency at which the list of UAPA Nodal Officers shall be circulated to all the Nodal Officers?
qa_pairs.answer: The list shall be circulated as and when the list is updated.

qa_pairs.question: What must the Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA cause to be done?
qa_pairs.answer: The Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA shall cause the amended list of UAPA Nodal Officers to be circulated to all the Nodal Officers.

qa_pairs.question: What must the Ministry of External Affairs do when the UNSC 1267 Committee or UNSC 1988 Committee revises the list of individuals and entities subject to UN sanction measures?
qa_pairs.answer: The Ministry of External Affairs shall update the list of individuals and entities subject to the UN sanction measures and electronically forward the changes without delay to the designated Nodal Officers.

qa_pairs.question: What is the time limit for the Financial Regulators to forward the list of designated persons to banks, stock exchanges/depositories, intermediaries regulated by SEBI and insurance companies?
qa_pairs.answer: The Financial Regulators shall forward the list of designated persons without delay.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the UAPA Nodal Officer in Foreigners Division of MHA not required to forward the designated list to the immigration authorities and security agencies?
qa_pairs.answer: The UAPA Nodal Officer in Foreigners Division of MHA is not required to forward the designated list to the immigration authorities and security agencies if the list is not revised by the UNSC 1267 Committee or UNSC 1988 Committee.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a designated Nodal Officer for the UAPA?
qa_pairs.answer: The Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA shall forward the designated list to all the UAPA Nodal Officers of States/UTs.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for the Regulators of the real estate agents, dealers in precious metals & stones (DPMS) and DNFBPs to forward the list of designated persons?
qa_pairs.answer: The Regulators of the real estate agents, dealers in precious metals & stones (DPMS) and DNFBPs shall forward the list of designated persons as mentioned in Para 4(i) above, to the real estate agents, dealers in precious metals & stones (DPMS) and DNFBPs without delay.

qa_pairs.question: What must the Financial Regulators do when they receive the list of designated persons from the Ministry of External Affairs?
qa_pairs.answer: The Financial Regulators shall forward the list of designated persons as mentioned in Para 4(i) above, without delay to the banks, stock exchanges/depositories, intermediaries regulated by SEBI and insurance companies.

qa_pairs.question: What is the time limit for the Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA to forward the designated list to all the UAPA Nodal Officers of States/UTs?
qa_pairs.answer: The Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA shall forward the designated list without delay.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the Regulators of the real estate agents, dealers in precious metals & stones (DPMS) and DNFBPs not required to forward the list of designated persons to the real estate agents, dealers in precious metals & stones (DPMS) and DNFBPs?
qa_pairs.answer: The Regulators of the real estate agents, dealers in precious metals & stones (DPMS) and DNFBPs are not required to forward the list of designated persons to the real estate agents, dealers in precious metals & stones (DPMS) and DNFBPs if the list is not revised by the UNSC 1267 Committee or UNSC 1988 Committee.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for the Ministry of External Affairs to update the list of individuals and entities subject to UN sanction measures?
qa_pairs.answer: The Ministry of External Affairs shall update the list of individuals and entities subject to the UN sanction measures and electronically forward the changes without delay to the designated Nodal Officers.

qa_pairs.question: What must banks do when they find a match with designated individuals/entities?
qa_pairs.answer: Banks must immediately inform full particulars of the funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services held by such customer on their books to the Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA, at Fax No.011-23092551 and also convey over telephone No. 011-23092548.

qa_pairs.question: What is the time limit for completing the verification by the State Police and/or the Central Agencies?
qa_pairs.answer: The verification would be completed expeditiously from the date of receipt of such particulars.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is a bank not required to prevent a designated person from conducting financial transactions?
qa_pairs.answer: The match of any of the customers with the particulars of designated individuals/entities is beyond doubt.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a designated individual/entity?
qa_pairs.answer: Individuals/entities listed in the Schedule to the Order.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for reporting a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) with FIU-IND?
qa_pairs.answer: The banks, stock exchanges/depositories, intermediaries regulated by SEBI, and insurance companies shall file a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) with FIU-IND covering all transactions in the accounts, covered under Paragraph 5.1(ii) above, carried through or attempted as per the prescribed format.

qa_pairs.question: What must banks do when they find a match with designated individuals/entities beyond doubt?
qa_pairs.answer: Banks must prevent such designated persons from conducting financial transactions, under intimation to the Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA at Fax No.011-23092551 and also convey over telephone No.011-23092548.

qa_pairs.question: What is the format for reporting a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) with FIU-IND?
qa_pairs.answer: As per the prescribed format.

qa_pairs.question: What must the Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA do when the results of the verification indicate that the properties are owned by or are held for the benefit of the designated individuals/entities?
qa_pairs.answer: An order to freeze these assets under Section 51A of the UAPA would be issued by the Central [designated] nodal officer for the UAPA without delay and conveyed electronically to the concerned bank branch, depository and insurance company under intimation to respective Regulators and FIU-IND.

qa_pairs.question: What must the Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA do when issuing an order to freeze assets under Section 51A of the UAPA?
qa_pairs.answer: The Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA shall also forward a copy thereof to all the Principal Secretaries/Secretaries, Home Department of the States/UTs and all UAPA nodal officers in the country, so that any individual or entity may be prohibited from making any funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services available for the benefit of the designated individuals/ entities or any other person engaged in or suspected to be engaged in terrorism.

qa_pairs.question: What must the Central Nodal Officer for the UAPA do with the designated list?
qa_pairs.answer: The Central Nodal Officer for the UAPA must electronically forward the designated list to the UAPA Nodal Officers of all States and UTs with a request to have the names of the designated individuals/entities verified from the records of the office of the Registrar performing the work of registration of immovable properties in their respective jurisdiction, without delay.

qa_pairs.question: What is the time limit for completing the verification by the State Police?
qa_pairs.answer: The verification by the State Police shall be completed within 24 hours of the verification, if it matches with the particulars of the designated individual/entity.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the prior notice to the designated individual/entity not required?
qa_pairs.answer: Prior notice to the designated individual/entity is not required when the Central Nodal Officer for the UAPA issues an order under Section 51A of the UAPA.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a designated individual/entity under this section?
qa_pairs.answer: Individuals/entities holding financial assets or economic resources of the nature of immovable property are designated individuals/entities under this section.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for monitoring transactions/accounts of the designated individual/entity?
qa_pairs.answer: The UAPA Nodal Officer of the State/UT shall cause to monitor the transactions/accounts of the designated individual/entity so as to prohibit any individual or entity from making any funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services available for the benefit of the individuals or entities listed in the Schedule to the Order or any other person engaged in or suspected to be engaged in terrorism.

qa_pairs.question: What are the communication channels for conveying the particulars of the designated individual/entity to the Central Nodal Officer for the UAPA?
qa_pairs.answer: The particulars apart from being sent by post would necessarily be conveyed on email id: jsctcr-mha@gov.in, and also on Fax No. 011-23092551 and telephone No. 011-23092548.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of conducting an inquiry by the State Police?
qa_pairs.answer: The purpose of conducting an inquiry by the State Police is to ensure that the particulars sent by the Registrar performing the work of registering immovable properties are indeed of the designated individuals/entities.

qa_pairs.question: What action shall be initiated by the DGP/Commissioner of Police of the State/UT upon becoming aware of any transactions and attempts by third party?
qa_pairs.answer: The DGP/Commissioner of Police of the State/UT shall initiate action under the provisions of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967, upon becoming aware of any transactions and attempts by third party.

qa_pairs.question: What is the method of verification that the Central Nodal Officer for the UAPA may also have conducted?
qa_pairs.answer: The Central Nodal Officer for the UAPA may also have the verification conducted by the Central Agencies.

qa_pairs.question: What must the Designated Non-Financial Businesses and Professions (DNFBPs) do when a designated individual/entity approaches them for a transaction or relationship?
qa_pairs.answer: The DNFBPs are required to inform the UAPA Nodal officer of the State/UT without delay, with details of the funds/assets held and the details of the transaction.

qa_pairs.question: What is the monetary/time limit for the DNFBPs to inform the UAPA Nodal officer of the State/UT?
qa_pairs.answer: The DNFBPs must inform the UAPA Nodal officer of the State/UT without delay.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is a society/firm/non-profit organization not required to be registered?
qa_pairs.answer: A society/firm/non-profit organization is not required to be registered if any of the designated individual/entity is a director/partner/officer bearer/trustee/settler/beneficiary or beneficial owner of such juridical person.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a Designated Non-Financial Businesses and Professions (DNFBPs)?
qa_pairs.answer: The Designated Non-Financial Businesses and Professions (DNFBPs) include casinos, real estate agents, dealers in precious metals/stones (DPMS), lawyers/notaries, accountants, company service providers and societies/firms and non-profit organizations.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for the UAPA Nodal Officer of the State/UT to follow when informed by the DNFBPs?
qa_pairs.answer: The UAPA Nodal Officer of the State/UT shall follow the procedure as laid down in paragraphs 6.2 to 6.5 above.

qa_pairs.question: What must the Casino owner do when a designated individual/entity visits or participates in any game in the Casino and/or if any assets of such designated individual/entity is with the Casino operator?
qa_pairs.answer: The Casino owner shall inform the UAPA Nodal Officer of the State/UT without delay, who shall in turn follow the procedure laid down in paragraph 6.2 to 6.5 above.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India, Institute of Cost and Works Accountants of India and Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI) to follow when informed by a designated individual/entity?
qa_pairs.answer: The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India, Institute of Cost and Works Accountants of India and Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI) shall convey the complete details of such designated individual/entity to UAPA Nodal Officer in the Ministry of Corporate Affairs who shall in turn follow the similar procedure as laid down in paragraph 6.2 to 6.5 above.

qa_pairs.question: What must the member of the ICSI do when a designated individual/entity is a Director and/or Shareholder or having beneficial ownership of any such juridical person?
qa_pairs.answer: The member of the ICSI shall convey the complete details of such designated individual/entity to UAPA Nodal Officer in the Ministry of Corporate Affairs who shall in turn follow the similar procedure as laid down in paragraph 6.2 to 6.5 above.

qa_pairs.question: What must any person, either directly or indirectly, holding any funds or other assets of designated individuals or entities do when a transaction is attempted?
qa_pairs.answer: Any person, either directly or indirectly, holding any funds or other assets of designated individuals or entities, shall, without delay and without prior notice, cause to freeze any transaction in relation to such funds or assets, by immediately informing the nearest Police Station, which shall, in turn, inform the concerned UAPA Nodal Officer of the State/UT along with the details of the funds/assets held.

qa_pairs.question: What must countries do when they receive a request from another country under U.N. Security Council Resolution 1373?
qa_pairs.answer: Countries must freeze without delay the funds or other assets of persons who commit, or attempt to commit, terrorist acts or participate in or facilitate the commission of terrorist acts. Each individual country has the authority to designate the persons and entities that should have their funds or other assets frozen.

qa_pairs.question: What is the time limit for the Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA to examine a request?
qa_pairs.answer: The Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA shall cause the request to be examined without delay.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is a country not required to freeze the funds or other assets of a person?
qa_pairs.answer: A country is not required to freeze the funds or other assets of a person if the request is not supported by reasonable grounds, or a reasonable basis, to suspect or believe that the proposed designee is a terrorist, one who finances terrorism or a terrorist organization.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a designated individual/entity under U.N. Security Council Resolution 1373?
qa_pairs.answer: A person or entity who commits, or attempts to commit, terrorist acts or participates in or facilitates the commission of terrorist acts, or is owned or controlled directly or indirectly by such persons, or acts on behalf of, or at the direction of such persons and entities, including funds or other assets derived or generated from property owned or controlled, directly or indirectly, by such persons and associated persons and entities.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for forwarding a request from a foreign country to the Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA?
qa_pairs.answer: The Ministry of External Affairs shall examine the requests made by the foreign countries and forward it electronically, with their comments, to the Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA for freezing of funds or other assets.

qa_pairs.question: What must the Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA do after examining a request?
qa_pairs.answer: The Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA shall request would be electronically forwarded to the Nodal Officers in Regulators, FIU-IND and to the Nodal Officers of the States/UTs after satisfying itself that the requested designation is supported by reasonable grounds, or a reasonable basis, to suspect or believe that the proposed designee is a terrorist, one who finances terrorism or a terrorist organization.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of countries examining and giving effect to the actions initiated under the freezing mechanisms of other countries?
qa_pairs.answer: To ensure that effective cooperation is developed among countries.

qa_pairs.question: What must the Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA do to satisfy itself that a requested designation is supported by reasonable grounds?
qa_pairs.answer: The Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA shall cause the request to be examined without delay, so as to satisfy itself that on the basis of applicable legal principles, the requested designation is supported by reasonable grounds, or a reasonable basis, to suspect or believe that the proposed designee is a terrorist, one who finances terrorism or a terrorist organization.

qa_pairs.question: What is the expected action of countries when they receive a request from another country under U.N. Security Council Resolution 1373, if the request is appropriate?
qa_pairs.answer: Countries should examine and give effect to, if appropriate, the actions initiated under the freezing mechanisms of other countries.

qa_pairs.question: What must Nodal Officers do upon receipt of requests from the Central designated Nodal Officer for the UAPA?
qa_pairs.answer: The similar procedure as enumerated at paragraphs 5 and 6 above shall be followed.

qa_pairs.question: What is the notice requirement for freezing orders issued by Nodal Officers?
qa_pairs.answer: The freezing orders shall be issued without prior notice to the designated persons involved.

qa_pairs.question: What is the monetary/time limit for issuing freezing orders by Nodal Officers?
qa_pairs.answer: There is no specified monetary/time limit for issuing freezing orders by Nodal Officers.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is prior notice to the designated persons involved not required for freezing orders?
qa_pairs.answer: Prior notice to the designated persons involved is not required for freezing orders issued by Nodal Officers.

qa_pairs.question: Who are the designated persons involved for freezing orders?
qa_pairs.answer: The designated persons involved for freezing orders are those to whom the freezing orders are issued.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for issuing freezing orders by Nodal Officers?
qa_pairs.answer: The procedure for issuing freezing orders by Nodal Officers is the similar procedure as enumerated at paragraphs 5 and 6 above.

qa_pairs.question: What is the role of the Central designated Nodal Officer for the UAPA in the freezing order process?
qa_pairs.answer: The Central designated Nodal Officer for the UAPA is responsible for submitting requests to the Nodal Officers for freezing orders.

qa_pairs.question: What must Nodal Officers do upon receipt of requests from the Central designated Nodal Officer for the UAPA?
qa_pairs.answer: The similar procedure as enumerated at paragraphs 5 and 6 above shall be followed.

qa_pairs.question: Are Nodal Officers required to provide prior notice to the designated persons involved for freezing orders?
qa_pairs.answer: No, Nodal Officers are not required to provide prior notice to the designated persons involved for freezing orders.

qa_pairs.question: What must the Central designated nodal officer of the UAPA determine for exemption?
qa_pairs.answer: The Central designated nodal officer of the UAPA must determine that funds and other financial assets or economic resources are necessary for basic expenses or exclusively for payment of reasonable professional fees and reimbursement of incurred expenses associated with the provision of legal services or fees or service charges for routine holding or maintenance of frozen funds or other financial assets or economic resources.

qa_pairs.question: What is the time limit for the Ministry of External Affairs to make a negative decision on notification?
qa_pairs.answer: The Ministry of External Affairs must make a negative decision within 48 hours of notification.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the addition of interest or other earnings due on frozen accounts allowed?
qa_pairs.answer: The addition of interest or other earnings due on frozen accounts is allowed subject to the provisions of paragraph 10 of the resolutions 1267 (1999), 1333 (2000), or 1390 (2002), provided that any such interest, other earnings continue to be subject to those provisions.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a designated individual or organization for submitting a request for exemption?
qa_pairs.answer: A designated individual or organization qualifies for submitting a request for exemption.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for submitting a request for exemption to the Central designated nodal officer of the UAPA?
qa_pairs.answer: The designated individual or organization may submit a request to the Central designated nodal officer of the UAPA by post at “Joint Secretary (CTCR), North Block, New Delhi – 110001” or through email to jsctcr-mha@gov.in”, and the Central designated nodal officer shall examine such requests in consultation with the Law Enforcement Agencies and other Security Agencies and Intelligence Agencies.

qa_pairs.question: What must the Central designated nodal officer of the UAPA communicate to the Ministry of External Affairs for notifying the committee established pursuant to UNSC Resolution 1267 (1999)?
qa_pairs.answer: The Central designated nodal officer of the UAPA must communicate the intention to authorize access to such funds, assets or resources in terms of Para 10.1 above, if applicable, to the Ministry of External Affairs for notifying the committee established pursuant to UNSC Resolution 1267 (1999).

qa_pairs.question: What is the address for submitting a request to the Central designated nodal officer of the UAPA by post?
qa_pairs.answer: The address for submitting a request to the Central designated nodal officer of the UAPA by post is “Joint Secretary (CTCR), North Block, New Delhi – 110001”.

qa_pairs.question: What is the time limit for the Central designated nodal officer of the UAPA to examine requests for exemption?
qa_pairs.answer: There is no specific time limit mentioned in the section for the Central designated nodal officer of the UAPA to examine requests for exemption.

qa_pairs.question: What must the Central designated nodal officer of the UAPA do in consultation with the Law Enforcement Agencies and other Security Agencies and Intelligence Agencies?
qa_pairs.answer: The Central designated nodal officer of the UAPA must examine requests for exemption in consultation with the Law Enforcement Agencies and other Security Agencies and Intelligence Agencies.

qa_pairs.question: What must an individual or entity do if they have evidence that their funds have been inadvertently frozen?
qa_pairs.answer: They shall move an application giving the requisite evidence, in writing, to the concerned bank, stock exchanges/depositories, intermediaries regulated by SEBI, insurance companies, Registrar of Immovable Properties, ROC, Regulators of DNFBPs and the UAPA Nodal Officers of State/UT.

qa_pairs.question: What is the time limit for banks to inform and forward a copy of the application to the Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA?
qa_pairs.answer: Within two working days.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is it not possible for the Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA to pass an order unfreezing the assets within 5 working days?
qa_pairs.answer: If it is not possible for any reason to pass an Order unfreezing the assets within 5 working days, the Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA shall inform the applicant expeditiously.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA?
qa_pairs.answer: The Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA shall cause such verification, as may be required on the basis of the evidence furnished by the individual/entity, and, if satisfied, he/she shall pass an order, without delay, unfreezing the funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services, owned/held by such applicant.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for unfreezing of funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services of individuals/entities inadvertently affected by the freezing mechanism?
qa_pairs.answer: The individual/entity shall move an application giving the requisite evidence, in writing, to the concerned bank, stock exchanges/depositories, intermediaries regulated by SEBI, insurance companies, Registrar of Immovable Properties, ROC, Regulators of DNFBPs and the UAPA Nodal Officers of State/UT. The banks shall inform and forward a copy of the application to the Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA within two working days. The Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA shall cause such verification, as may be required on the basis of the evidence furnished by the individual/entity, and, if satisfied, he/she shall pass an order, without delay, unfreezing the funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services, owned/held by such applicant.

qa_pairs.question: What details must be given by any individual or entity informing of the funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services have been frozen inadvertently?
qa_pairs.answer: The full details of the asset frozen.

qa_pairs.question: What is the time limit for the Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA to pass an order unfreezing the funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services, owned/held by the applicant?
qa_pairs.answer: Without delay.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions shall the Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA inform the applicant expeditiously?
qa_pairs.answer: If it is not possible for any reason to pass an Order unfreezing the assets within 5 working days.

qa_pairs.question: What must the banks, stock exchanges/depositories, intermediaries regulated by SEBI, insurance companies, Registrar of Immovable Properties, ROC, Regulators of DNFBPs and the State/ UT Nodal Officers do when they receive an application from an individual or entity?
qa_pairs.answer: They shall inform and forward a copy of the application together with full details of the asset frozen to the Central [designated] Nodal Officer for the UAPA within two working days.
