qa_pairs.question: What must the UAPA Nodal Officer in the Foreigners Division of MHA do regarding designated individuals?
qa_pairs.answer: The UAPA Nodal Officer shall forward the designated lists to the immigration authorities and security agencies with a request to prevent the entry into or the transit through India.

qa_pairs.question: What is the requirement for prior notice to the designated individuals/entities?
qa_pairs.answer: The order shall take place without prior notice to the designated individuals/entities.

qa_pairs.question: What must the immigration authorities ensure regarding the order?
qa_pairs.answer: The immigration authorities shall ensure strict compliance of the order.

qa_pairs.question: What details must the immigration authorities communicate to the UAPA Nodal Officer?
qa_pairs.answer: The immigration authorities shall communicate the details of entry or transit through India of the designated individuals as prevented by them to the UAPA Nodal Officer in Foreigners Division of MHA.

qa_pairs.question: What is the threshold for the UAPA Nodal Officer to forward the designated lists?
qa_pairs.answer: There is no specific monetary or time limit mentioned for the UAPA Nodal Officer to forward the designated lists.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is prior notice to the designated individuals/entities not required?
qa_pairs.answer: Prior notice to the designated individuals/entities is not required when the order is made without prior notice.

qa_pairs.question: Who is responsible for ensuring strict compliance of the order?
qa_pairs.answer: The immigration authorities are responsible for ensuring strict compliance of the order.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for the immigration authorities to communicate the details of entry or transit through India of the designated individuals?
qa_pairs.answer: The immigration authorities shall communicate the details of entry or transit through India of the designated individuals as prevented by them to the UAPA Nodal Officer in Foreigners Division of MHA.

qa_pairs.question: What must the Central designated Nodal Officer do?
qa_pairs.answer: The Central designated Nodal Officer must communicate the compliance of action taken under the UAPA.

qa_pairs.question: What is the role of the Nodal Officer for the UAPA?
qa_pairs.answer: The Nodal Officer for the UAPA is the Central designated Nodal Officer.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the Nodal Officer not required to communicate compliance?
qa_pairs.answer: There is no information provided on the conditions under which the Nodal Officer is not required to communicate compliance.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for communication of compliance of action taken under the UAPA?
qa_pairs.answer: The procedure for communication of compliance of action taken under the UAPA is not specified in this section.

qa_pairs.question: What is the Central designated Nodal Officer responsible for?
qa_pairs.answer: The Central designated Nodal Officer is responsible for communicating the compliance of action taken under the UAPA.

qa_pairs.question: Is the Nodal Officer for the UAPA the same as the Central designated Nodal Officer?
qa_pairs.answer: Yes, the Nodal Officer for the UAPA is the Central designated Nodal Officer.

qa_pairs.question: What must the Nodal Officer for the UAPA do?
qa_pairs.answer: The Nodal Officer for the UAPA must communicate the compliance of action taken under the UAPA.

qa_pairs.question: Is the Central designated Nodal Officer responsible for communicating compliance under the UAPA?
qa_pairs.answer: Yes, the Central designated Nodal Officer is responsible for communicating compliance under the UAPA.

qa_pairs.question: What must the Officer in the Foreigners Division, MHA do with the details of funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services of designated individuals/entities frozen by an order?
qa_pairs.answer: The Officer in the Foreigners Division, MHA must furnish the details to the Ministry of External Affairs for onward communication to the United Nations. Under Section 51.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of furnishing the details of individuals whose entry into India or transit through India was prevented?
qa_pairs.answer: The purpose is to enable the Ministry of External Affairs to communicate the details to the United Nations. Under Section 51.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the Officer in the Foreigners Division, MHA not required to furnish the details of funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services of designated individuals/entities frozen by an order?
qa_pairs.answer: There is no exception mentioned in Section 51. The Officer in the Foreigners Division, MHA must furnish the details. Under Section 51.

qa_pairs.question: What is the process for furnishing the details of funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services of designated individuals/entities frozen by an order?
qa_pairs.answer: The Officer in the Foreigners Division, MHA shall furnish the details to the Ministry of External Affairs for onward communication to the United Nations. Under Section 51.

qa_pairs.question: What is the threshold for the Officer in the Foreigners Division, MHA to furnish the details of funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services of designated individuals/entities frozen by an order?
qa_pairs.answer: There is no monetary or time limit mentioned in Section 51. The Officer in the Foreigners Division, MHA must furnish the details. Under Section 51.

qa_pairs.question: Who is responsible for receiving the details furnished by the Officer in the Foreigners Division, MHA?
qa_pairs.answer: The Ministry of External Affairs is responsible for receiving the details for onward communication to the United Nations. Under Section 51.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of furnishing the details of funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services of designated individuals/entities frozen by an order to the Ministry of External Affairs?
qa_pairs.answer: The purpose is to enable the Ministry of External Affairs to communicate the details to the United Nations. Under Section 51.

qa_pairs.question: What must the Ministry of External Affairs do with the details furnished by the Officer in the Foreigners Division, MHA?
qa_pairs.answer: The Ministry of External Affairs must communicate the details to the United Nations. Under Section 51.

qa_pairs.question: What is the process for the Ministry of External Affairs to communicate the details to the United Nations?
qa_pairs.answer: The Ministry of External Affairs shall receive the details from the Officer in the Foreigners Division, MHA and communicate them to the United Nations. Under Section 51.

qa_pairs.question: What must the Central designated Nodal Officer for the UAPA do when issuing an order under Section 51A of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967?
qa_pairs.answer: The order shall be communicated to all the UAPA nodal officers in the country, the Regulators of Financial Services, FIU-IND and DNFBPs, banks, depositories/stock exchanges, intermediaries regulated by SEBI, Registrars performing the work of registering immovable properties through the UAPA Nodal Officer of the State/UT.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the Central designated Nodal Officer for the UAPA not required to communicate the order to the UAPA nodal officers in the country?
qa_pairs.answer: There are no conditions specified in the section for not communicating the order to the UAPA nodal officers in the country. The order shall be communicated to all the UAPA nodal officers in the country.

qa_pairs.question: Who must be communicated the order issued under Section 51A of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967?
qa_pairs.answer: The order shall be communicated to all the UAPA nodal officers in the country, the Regulators of Financial Services, FIU-IND and DNFBPs, banks, depositories/stock exchanges, intermediaries regulated by SEBI, Registrars performing the work of registering immovable properties through the UAPA Nodal Officer of the State/UT.

qa_pairs.question: What is the definition of the entities that must be communicated the order issued under Section 51A of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967?
qa_pairs.answer: The entities include UAPA nodal officers in the country, the Regulators of Financial Services, FIU-IND and DNFBPs, banks, depositories/stock exchanges, intermediaries regulated by SEBI, Registrars performing the work of registering immovable properties through the UAPA Nodal Officer of the State/UT.

qa_pairs.question: What is the process for communicating the order issued under Section 51A of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967?
qa_pairs.answer: The order shall be communicated through the UAPA Nodal Officer of the State/UT to all the entities listed in the section.

qa_pairs.question: What is the threshold for the entities that must be communicated the order issued under Section 51A of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967?
qa_pairs.answer: There is no monetary or time limit specified in the section for the entities that must be communicated the order.

qa_pairs.question: What is the definition of the Central designated Nodal Officer for the UAPA?
qa_pairs.answer: The Central designated Nodal Officer for the UAPA is the officer designated by the Central government for the purpose of issuing orders under Section 51A of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967.

qa_pairs.question: What must the Regulators of Financial Services, FIU-IND and DNFBPs, banks, depositories/stock exchanges, intermediaries regulated by SEBI, Registrars performing the work of registering immovable properties do when they receive the order issued under Section 51A of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967?
qa_pairs.answer: There is no specific action mentioned in the section for these entities when they receive the order.

qa_pairs.question: What must the RBI Governor do when receiving this order?
qa_pairs.answer: The RBI Governor must ensure strict compliance of this order.

qa_pairs.question: Who is requested to ensure strict compliance of this order?
qa_pairs.answer: All concerned are requested to ensure strict compliance of this order.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of sending this order to multiple authorities?
qa_pairs.answer: The purpose is to ensure strict compliance of this order across various departments and institutions.

qa_pairs.question: What is the role of the Joint Secretary to the Government of India in this order?
qa_pairs.answer: The Joint Secretary to the Government of India is the sender of this order.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for sending this order to the RBI Governor?
qa_pairs.answer: The order is sent directly to the RBI Governor.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of sending a copy of this order for information to other authorities?
qa_pairs.answer: The purpose is to keep them informed about the order.

qa_pairs.question: Is there a specific time limit for ensuring compliance with this order?
qa_pairs.answer: No specific time limit is mentioned in the order.

qa_pairs.question: Is there an exception to the requirement of ensuring strict compliance of this order?
qa_pairs.answer: No exception is mentioned in the order.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when implementing Section 12A of the Weapons of Mass Destruction and their Delivery Systems (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Act, 2005?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities must follow the procedure as specified in the order dated 1 September, 2023, issued by the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, Government of India.

qa_pairs.question: What is the monetary limit for the implementation of Section 12A of the Weapons of Mass Destruction and their Delivery Systems (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Act, 2005?
qa_pairs.answer: No monetary limit is specified in the order dated 1 September, 2023, for the implementation of Section 12A.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the procedure for implementation of Section 12A of the Weapons of Mass Destruction and their Delivery Systems (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Act, 2005 not required?
qa_pairs.answer: The procedure is not required for implementation of Section 12A, as specified in the order dated 1 September, 2023, issued by the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, Government of India.

qa_pairs.question: Who is responsible for issuing the order for implementation of Section 12A of the Weapons of Mass Destruction and their Delivery Systems (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Act, 2005?
qa_pairs.answer: The order for implementation of Section 12A is issued by the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, Government of India.

qa_pairs.question: What is the date of the order for implementation of Section 12A of the Weapons of Mass Destruction and their Delivery Systems (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Act, 2005?
qa_pairs.answer: The order is dated 1 September, 2023.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for implementation of Section 12A of the Weapons of Mass Destruction and their Delivery Systems (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Act, 2005?
qa_pairs.answer: The procedure is specified in the order dated 1 September, 2023, issued by the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, Government of India.

qa_pairs.question: What document specifies the procedure for implementation of Section 12A of the Weapons of Mass Destruction and their Delivery Systems (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Act, 2005?
qa_pairs.answer: The procedure is specified in the order dated 1 September, 2023, issued by the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, Government of India.

qa_pairs.question: What is the name of the Act that Section 12A is a part of?
qa_pairs.answer: The Weapons of Mass Destruction and their Delivery Systems (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Act, 2005.

qa_pairs.question: What is the name of the department that issued the order for implementation of Section 12A of the Weapons of Mass Destruction and their Delivery Systems (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Act, 2005?
qa_pairs.answer: The Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, Government of India.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when they suspect an activity is prohibited under the Act?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities must prevent financing of such activities by freezing, seizing or attaching funds or other financial assets or economic resources owned or controlled by the person.

qa_pairs.question: What is the monetary/time limit for freezing funds under Section 12?
qa_pairs.answer: There is no specific monetary/time limit mentioned in Section 12 for freezing funds.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the Central Government not required to freeze funds under Section 12?
qa_pairs.answer: The Central Government is not required to freeze funds if it exercises its powers through an authority assigned under sub-section (1) of section 7.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a person related to any activity prohibited under the Act?
qa_pairs.answer: The Act does not explicitly define a person related to any prohibited activity, but it implies that it includes individuals or entities connected to the prohibited activity.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for exercising powers under Section 12?
qa_pairs.answer: The Central Government may exercise its powers under Section 12 through any authority assigned the power under sub-section (1) of section 7.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of Section 12?
qa_pairs.answer: The purpose of Section 12 is to prevent financing of activities prohibited under the Act, the United Nations (Security Council) Act, 1947, or any other relevant Act.

qa_pairs.question: What types of financial assets or economic resources can be frozen under Section 12?
qa_pairs.answer: Funds or other financial assets or economic resources owned or controlled, wholly or jointly, directly or indirectly, by the person can be frozen under Section 12.

qa_pairs.question: What is the effect of freezing funds under Section 12?
qa_pairs.answer: Freezing funds under Section 12 prohibits any person from making funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services available for the benefit of the person.

qa_pairs.question: What is the power of the Central Government under Section 12?
qa_pairs.answer: The Central Government has the power to freeze, seize or attach funds or other financial assets or economic resources, or prohibit any person from making funds available for the benefit of persons related to prohibited activities.

qa_pairs.question: What must the Central Government do under Section 7(1) of the Act?
qa_pairs.answer: The Central Government assigns Director, FIU-India, Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, as the authority to exercise powers under Section 12A of the Act.

qa_pairs.question: What is the definition of Regulator under this order?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulator shall have the same meaning as defined in Rule 2(fa) of Prevention of Money-Laundering (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005.

qa_pairs.question: What is the definition of Reporting under this order?
qa_pairs.answer: Reporting shall have the same meaning as defined in Section 2 (1) (wa) of Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002.

qa_pairs.question: What is the definition of DNFPBs under this order?
qa_pairs.answer: DNFPBs is as defined in section 2(1) (sa) of Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for notifying a Nodal Officer for implementation of provisions of Section 12A of the Act?
qa_pairs.answer: The Regulators, Ministry of Corporate Affairs and Foreigners Division of MHA shall notify a Nodal Officer for implementation of provisions of Section 12A of the Act.

qa_pairs.question: What is the contact information of the Central Nodal Officer (CNO)?
qa_pairs.answer: The Central Nodal Officer (CNO) can be contacted at Telephone Number: 011- 23314458, 011- 23314435, 011- 23314459 (FAX), email address: dir@fiuindia.gov.in.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the appointment of a Nodal Officer not required?
qa_pairs.answer: The appointment of a Nodal Officer is not required under this order.

qa_pairs.question: What is the definition of DNFPBs under this order?
qa_pairs.answer: DNFPBs is as defined in section 2(1) (sa) of Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002.

qa_pairs.question: What is the definition of Reporting under this order?
qa_pairs.answer: Reporting shall have the same meaning as defined in Section 2 (1) (wa) of Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002.

qa_pairs.question: What must all the States and UTs do?
qa_pairs.answer: All the States and UTs shall notify a State Nodal officer for implementation of Section 12A of the Act.

qa_pairs.question: What is the role of the Nodal Officer?
qa_pairs.answer: The Nodal Officer is also the Nodal Officer for implementation of Section 12A of the Act.

qa_pairs.question: What is the Act that the Nodal Officer is responsible for?
qa_pairs.answer: The Act is UAPA.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of notifying a State Nodal officer?
qa_pairs.answer: The purpose is for implementation of Section 12A of the Act.

qa_pairs.question: Under what Act is the Nodal Officer appointed?
qa_pairs.answer: The Nodal Officer is appointed under A of UAPA.

qa_pairs.question: What is the role of the Nodal Officer under Section 12A of the Act?
qa_pairs.answer: The Nodal Officer is responsible for implementation of Section 12A of the Act.

qa_pairs.question: What is the Nodal Officer responsible for implementing?
qa_pairs.answer: The Nodal Officer is responsible for implementing Section 12A of the Act.

qa_pairs.question: What must the States and UTs notify for implementation of Section 12A of the Act?
qa_pairs.answer: The States and UTs must notify a State Nodal officer.

qa_pairs.question: What must the CNO do with the updated list of Nodal Officers?
qa_pairs.answer: The CNO shall share the updated list with all Nodal Officers periodically and forward the updated list to all REs.

qa_pairs.question: What is the frequency of sharing the updated list of Nodal Officers by the CNO?
qa_pairs.answer: The CNO shall share the updated list with all Nodal Officers periodically.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the CNO not required to share the updated list of Nodal Officers?
qa_pairs.answer: There is no exception mentioned in this section.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a Nodal Officer under Section 12 of the Act?
qa_pairs.answer: A State/UT may notify the State Nodal Officer appointed for implementation of provisions of Section 51A of UAPA, also, as the Nodal Officer for implementation of Section 12A of the Act.

qa_pairs.question: What is the process for maintaining an updated list of Nodal Officers by the CNO?
qa_pairs.answer: The CNO shall maintain an updated list of all Nodal Officers.

qa_pairs.question: What must the CNO do with the list of Nodal Officers appointed under Section 51A of UAPA?
qa_pairs.answer: A State/UT may notify the State Nodal Officer appointed for implementation of provisions of Section 51A of UAPA, also, as the Nodal Officer for implementation of Section 12A of the Act.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of sharing the updated list of Nodal Officers by the CNO?
qa_pairs.answer: The CNO shall share the updated list with all Nodal Officers periodically and forward the updated list to all REs.

qa_pairs.question: What is the responsibility of the CNO in relation to the Nodal Officers?
qa_pairs.answer: The CNO shall maintain an updated list of all Nodal Officers and share the updated list with all Nodal Officers periodically.

qa_pairs.question: What is the process for forwarding the updated list of Nodal Officers by the CNO to REs?
qa_pairs.answer: The CNO shall forward the updated list of all Nodal Officers to all REs.

qa_pairs.question: What must the Ministry of External Affairs do when there are changes in the list of designated individuals and entities?
qa_pairs.answer: The Ministry of External Affairs must electronically communicate, without delay, the changes made in the list of designated individuals and entities to the CNO and Nodal officers.

qa_pairs.question: What is the time limit for the CNO to update the Designated list on the portal of FIU-India?
qa_pairs.answer: The CNO shall update the Designated list without delay, as and when it is updated.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the Ministry of External Affairs permitted to share other information relating to prohibition / prevention of financing of prohibited activity?
qa_pairs.answer: The Ministry of External Affairs may share other information relating to prohibition / prevention of financing of prohibited activity under Section 12A (after its initial assessment of the relevant factors in the case) with the CNO and other organizations concerned.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a Nodal Officer for Section 12A in Foreigners Division of MHA?
qa_pairs.answer: The Nodal Officer for Section 12A in Foreigners Division of MHA shall forward the updated designated list to the immigration authorities and security agencies, without delay.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for making the updated designated list available to the Regulators?
qa_pairs.answer: The Regulators shall make available the updated designated list, without delay, to their REs.

qa_pairs.question: What must the CNO make available to the State Nodal Officers and Registrars performing the work of registration of immovable properties?
qa_pairs.answer: The CNO shall make available the updated designated list, without delay, to the State Nodal Officers and to the Registrars performing the work of registration of immovable properties.

qa_pairs.question: What is the time limit for the Regulators to make the updated designated list available to their REs?
qa_pairs.answer: The Regulators shall make available the updated designated list, without delay, to their REs.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the CNO not required to update the Designated list on the portal of FIU-India?
qa_pairs.answer: The CNO is not required to update the Designated list on the portal of FIU-India unless changes are made as per para 2.1 above.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for the Nodal Officer for Section 12A in Foreigners Division of MHA to forward the updated designated list to the immigration authorities and security agencies?
qa_pairs.answer: The Nodal Officer for Section 12A in Foreigners Division of MHA shall forward the updated designated list to the immigration authorities and security agencies, without delay.

qa_pairs.question: What must Financial Institutions do when the particulars of the entities/individual, party to the financial transactions, match with the particulars of the designated list?
qa_pairs.answer: Financial Institutions shall not carry out such transaction and shall immediately inform the transaction details with full particulars of the funds, financial assets or economic resources involved to the CNO by email, FAX and by post, without delay.

qa_pairs.question: What is the frequency at which Financial Institutions must run a check on the given parameters to verify whether individuals and entities in the designated list are holding any funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services?
qa_pairs.answer: Financial Institutions must run a check at the time of establishing a relation with a customer and on a periodic basis.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is a Financial Institution not required to carry out a transaction?
qa_pairs.answer: A Financial Institution is not required to carry out a transaction if the particulars of the entities/individual, party to the financial transactions, match with the particulars of the designated list.

qa_pairs.question: Who must be informed by Financial Institutions when the particulars of any of their customers match with the particulars of the designated list?
qa_pairs.answer: Financial Institutions must inform the CNO, State Nodal Officer, and their Regulator, as the case may be, without delay.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for informing the CNO, State Nodal Officer, and Regulator when the particulars of any of their customers match with the designated list?
qa_pairs.answer: Financial Institutions must inform the CNO, State Nodal Officer, and their Regulator, as the case may be, by email, FAX and by post, without delay.

qa_pairs.question: What must Financial Institutions do when there are reasons to believe beyond doubt that funds or assets held by a customer would fall under the purview of clause (a) or (b) of sub-section (2)?
qa_pairs.answer: Financial Institutions must inform the CNO, State Nodal Officer, and their Regulator, as the case may be, without delay.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of sending a copy of the communication to State Nodal Officer and Regulator?
qa_pairs.answer: The purpose is to inform them of the match with the designated list, as per the communication mentioned in 3.1 (i) and (ii) above.

qa_pairs.question: What is the method of communication for informing the CNO, State Nodal Officer, and Regulator?
qa_pairs.answer: Financial Institutions must inform them by email, FAX and by post, without delay.

qa_pairs.question: What is the action required to be taken by Financial Institutions when they have reasons to believe that funds or assets held by a customer would fall under the purview of clause (a) or (b) of sub-section (2)?
qa_pairs.answer: Financial Institutions must inform the CNO, State Nodal Officer, and their Regulator, as the case may be, without delay.

qa_pairs.question: What must REs do when they identify an individual/entity on the designated list?
qa_pairs.answer: REs shall prevent such individual/entity from conducting financial transactions, under intimation to the CNO by email, FAX and by post, without delay.

qa_pairs.question: What is the timeframe for completing the verification conducted by the State Police and/or the Central Agencies?
qa_pairs.answer: This verification would be completed expeditiously from the date of receipt of such particulars.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is prior notice to the designated individual/entity not required?
qa_pairs.answer: The order shall be issued without prior notice to the designated individual/entity.

qa_pairs.question: Who is responsible for conducting the verification?
qa_pairs.answer: The CNO would cause a verification to be conducted by the State Police and/or the Central Agencies.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for issuing an order to freeze assets under Section 12A?
qa_pairs.answer: An order to freeze these assets under Section 12A would be issued by the CNO without delay and be conveyed electronically to the concerned RE under intimation to respective Regulators.

qa_pairs.question: What must the CNO do after issuing an order to freeze assets?
qa_pairs.answer: The CNO shall also forward a copy thereof to all the Principal Secretaries/Secretaries, Home Department of the States/UTs and All Nodal officers in the country, so that any individual or entity may be prohibited from making any funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services available for the benefit of the designated individuals/entities.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of the verification conducted by the State Police and/or the Central Agencies?
qa_pairs.answer: so as to ensure that the individuals/entities identified by the REs are the ones in designated list and the funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services, reported by REs are in respect of the designated individuals/entities.

qa_pairs.question: What must the CNO forward to all Directors General of Police/ Commissioners of Police of all States/UTs after issuing an order to freeze assets?
qa_pairs.answer: The CNO shall also forward a copy of the order to all Directors General of Police/ Commissioners of Police of all States/UTs for initiating suitable action.

qa_pairs.question: What is the method of communication for conveying the order to freeze assets to the concerned RE?
qa_pairs.answer: be conveyed electronically to the concerned RE under intimation to respective Regulators.

qa_pairs.question: What must Registrars do when the particulars of entities/individuals match with the designated list?
qa_pairs.answer: Registrars shall not carry out such transaction and immediately inform the details with full particulars of the assets or economic resources involved to the State Nodal Officer, without delay.

qa_pairs.question: What is the time limit for the State Nodal Officer to cause communication of the complete particulars to the CNO?
qa_pairs.answer: The State Nodal Officer would cause communication of the complete particulars without delay by email, FAX and by post.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the Registrar not required to prevent an individual/entity from conducting transactions?
qa_pairs.answer: The Registrar is not required to prevent an individual/entity from conducting transactions if there are no reasons to believe beyond doubt that assets that are held by an individual/entity would fall under the purview of clause (a) or (b) of sub-section (2) of Section 12A.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a designated individual/entity for the purposes of this section?
qa_pairs.answer: The designated individuals/entities are those whose particulars match with the particulars in the designated list.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for conducting verification by the State Police?
qa_pairs.answer: The State Nodal Officer may cause such inquiry to be conducted by the State Police so as to ensure that the particulars sent are indeed of these designated individuals/entities. This verification shall be completed without delay and shall be conveyed, within 24 hours of the verification, if it matches, with the particulars of the designated individual/entity, to the CNO without delay by email, FAX and by post.

qa_pairs.question: What must the CNO do if the results of the verification indicate that the assets are owned by, or are held for the benefit of, the designated individuals/entities?
qa_pairs.answer: The CNO shall issue an order to freeze these assets under Section 12A without delay and be conveyed electronically to the concerned Registrar performing the work of registering immovable properties, and to FIU under intimation to the concerned State Nodal Officer.

qa_pairs.question: What is the time limit for the verification to be completed by the State Police?
qa_pairs.answer: The verification shall be completed without delay and shall be conveyed, within 24 hours of the verification, if it matches, with the particulars of the designated individual/entity, to the CNO without delay by email, FAX and by post.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions may the CNO have the verification conducted by the Central Agencies?
qa_pairs.answer: The CNO may also have the verification conducted by the Central Agencies. This verification would be completed expeditiously.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for issuing an order to freeze assets under Section 12A?
qa_pairs.answer: The CNO shall issue an order to freeze these assets under Section 12A without delay and be conveyed electronically to the concerned Registrar performing the work of registering immovable properties, and to FIU under intimation to the concerned State Nodal Officer. The CNO shall also forward a copy thereof to all the Principal Secretaries/Secretaries, Home Department of the States/UTs and All Nodal officers in the country, so that any individual or entity may be prohibited from making any funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services available for the benefit of the designated individuals / entities.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when dealing with real-estate agents?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities must verify the real-estate agents as per the notified rules under clause (vi) of PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005.

qa_pairs.question: What is the threshold for dealers of precious metals/stones (DPMS) to be notified under PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005?
qa_pairs.answer: The threshold for dealers of precious metals/stones (DPMS) to be notified under PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005 is not explicitly mentioned in this section.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the verification of Registrar of Societies/Firms/non-profit organizations not required?
qa_pairs.answer: The verification of Registrar of Societies/Firms/non-profit organizations is not required under this section, but it may be required under other sections or rules.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a Designated Non-Financial Businesses and Professions (DNFBPs) under this section?
qa_pairs.answer: The Ministry of Corporate Affairs qualifies as a Designated Non-Financial Businesses and Professions (DNFBPs) under this section.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for verifying real-estate agents as notified under clause (vi) of PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005?
qa_pairs.answer: The procedure for verifying real-estate agents as notified under clause (vi) of PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005 is not explicitly mentioned in this section.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when dealing with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities must verify the Ministry of Corporate Affairs as per the notified rules under this section.

qa_pairs.question: What is the threshold for real-estate agents to be notified under clause (vi) of PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005?
qa_pairs.answer: The threshold for real-estate agents to be notified under clause (vi) of PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005 is not explicitly mentioned in this section.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the verification of Designated Non-Financial Businesses and Professions (DNFBPs) not required?
qa_pairs.answer: The verification of Designated Non-Financial Businesses and Professions (DNFBPs) is not required under this section, but it may be required under other sections or rules.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for verifying dealers of precious metals/stones (DPMS) as notified under PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005?
qa_pairs.answer: The procedure for verifying dealers of precious metals/stones (DPMS) as notified under PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005 is not explicitly mentioned in this section.

qa_pairs.question: What must regulated entities do when a designated individual/entity approaches them for a transaction?
qa_pairs.answer: Regulated entities must not carry out the transaction and, without delay, inform the Section 12A Nodal officer in the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC).

qa_pairs.question: What is the monetary/time limit for freezing transactions related to designated individuals/entities?
qa_pairs.answer: There is no specific monetary/time limit mentioned in the section, but regulated entities must freeze transactions without delay.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is a society/firm/non-profit organization not required to freeze transactions for a designated individual/entity?
qa_pairs.answer: A society/firm/non-profit organization is not required to freeze transactions if it does not hold funds or assets of the designated individual/entity. However, it must still inform the State Nodal Officer without delay.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a designated individual/entity under Section 2?
qa_pairs.answer: A designated individual/entity includes any individual or entity listed in the 'designated list' referred to in Para 2.1, as well as any individual or entity acting on behalf of or at the direction of such individuals or entities.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for informing the Section 12A Nodal officer in the Ministry of Corporate Affairs?
qa_pairs.answer: The procedure involves conveying the complete details of the designated individual/entity, including the details of funds and assets held and the details of the transaction, without delay.

qa_pairs.question: What must the Registrar of Societies/Firms/non-profit organizations do when a designated individual/entity is a shareholder/member/partner/director/settler/trustee/beneficiary/beneficial owner of any society/partnership firm/trust/non-profit organization?
qa_pairs.answer: The Registrar must freeze any transaction for the designated individual/entity and inform the State Nodal Officer without delay.

qa_pairs.question: What is the role of the State Nodal Officer in monitoring transactions/accounts of designated individuals/entities?
qa_pairs.answer: The State Nodal Officer must cause to monitor the transactions/accounts of designated individuals/entities to prohibit any individual or entity from making funds, financial assets, or economic resources available for the benefit of individuals/entities in the designated list.

qa_pairs.question: What must the State Nodal Officer do upon becoming aware of any transactions and attempts by third parties?
qa_pairs.answer: The State Nodal Officer must, without delay, bring the incidence to the notice of the CNO and the DGP/Commissioner of Police of the State/UT for initiating suitable action.

qa_pairs.question: What is the obligation of all natural and legal persons holding funds or other assets of designated individuals/entities?
qa_pairs.answer: They must, without delay and without prior notice, freeze any transaction in relation to such funds or assets and immediately inform the State Nodal officer along with details of the funds/assets held.

qa_pairs.question: What must the CNO do when freezing funds or assets under Section 12A?
qa_pairs.answer: The CNO shall freeze such funds or Assets, without any delay, and make such order available to authorities, Financial Institutions, DNFBPs and other entities concerned.

qa_pairs.question: What is the monetary/time limit for freezing funds or assets under Section 12?
qa_pairs.answer: There is no specific monetary/time limit mentioned for freezing funds or assets under Section 12.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is the CNO not required to freeze funds or assets under Section 12?
qa_pairs.answer: The CNO is not required to freeze funds or assets if there is no delay in doing so, and the order is made available to authorities, Financial Institutions, DNFBPs and other entities concerned.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a person to whom the CNO can issue advisories and guidance under Section 12?
qa_pairs.answer: The CNO can issue advisories and guidance to all persons, including Fls and DNFBPs obligated to carry out sanctions screening.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for issuing advisories and guidance under Section 12?
qa_pairs.answer: The CNO shall have the power to issue advisories and guidance to all persons, including Fls and DNFBPs obligated to carry out sanctions screening.

qa_pairs.question: What action must the concerned Regulators take under their relevant laws, rules or regulations for each violation of sanction screening obligations under Section 12A?
qa_pairs.answer: The concerned Regulators shall take suitable action under their relevant laws, rules or regulations for each violation of sanction screening obligations under section 12A of the WMD Act.

qa_pairs.question: What must the concerned Regulators do for each violation of sanction screening obligations under Section 12A?
qa_pairs.answer: The concerned Regulators shall take suitable action under their relevant laws, rules or regulations for each violation of sanction screening obligations under section 12A of the WMD Act.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of the concerned Regulators taking action under their relevant laws, rules or regulations for each violation of sanction screening obligations under Section 12A?
qa_pairs.answer: The purpose is to take suitable action under their relevant laws, rules or regulations for each violation of sanction screening obligations under section 12A of the WMD Act.

qa_pairs.question: What is the effect of the CNO issuing advisories and guidance under Section 12?
qa_pairs.answer: The CNO shall have the power to issue advisories and guidance to all persons, including Fls and DNFBPs obligated to carry out sanctions screening.

qa_pairs.question: What must the CNO determine for exemption from freezing action?
qa_pairs.answer: The CNO must determine that the contract is not related to any of the prohibited goods, services, technologies, or activities, under this Act, or under the United Nations (Security Council) Act, 1947 or any other relevant Act for the time being in force, or by an order issued under any such Act, in relation to weapons of mass destruction and their delivery systems.

qa_pairs.question: What is the time limit for the UNSC or its Committee to respond to notification by the MEA?
qa_pairs.answer: The UNSC or its Committee must respond within 5 working days of such notification.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is a designated individual or entity allowed to make payments due under a contract entered into prior to listing?
qa_pairs.answer: A designated individual or entity is allowed to make payments due under a contract entered into prior to listing, provided that the CNO has determined that the contract is not related to any of the prohibited goods, services, technologies, or activities, and the MEA has submitted prior notification to the UNSC or its Committee, of the intention to make or receive such payments, ten working days prior to such authorization.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a designated individual or entity for the purposes of this Order?
qa_pairs.answer: This section does not explicitly define who qualifies as a designated individual or entity, but it is implied to be individuals or entities subject to the provisions of section 12A of the Act.

qa_pairs.question: What is the process for allowing designated individuals/entities to be credited with interest or other earnings due on their accounts?
qa_pairs.answer: The accounts of the designated individuals/entities may be allowed to be credited with interest or other earnings due on those accounts, or payments due under contracts, agreements or obligations that arose prior to the date on which those accounts became subject to the provisions of section 12A of the Act, provided that any such interest, other earnings and payments continue to be subject to those provisions under para 3.3.

qa_pairs.question: What must the MEA notify to the UNSC or its Committee for extraordinary expenses?
qa_pairs.answer: The MEA must notify the UNSC or its Committee of the determination of extraordinary expenses, and obtain approval from the UNSC or its Committee.

qa_pairs.question: What is the monetary limit for basic expenses that may be exempt from freezing action?
qa_pairs.answer: This section does not specify a monetary limit for basic expenses, but it implies that expenses for basic necessities such as foodstuff, rent or mortgage, medicines and medical treatment, taxes, insurance premiums and public utility charges, or reasonable professional fees and reimbursement of incurred expenses associated with the provision of legal services or fees or service charges for routine holding or maintenance of frozen funds or other financial assets or economic resources, may be exempt.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is a designated individual or entity allowed to make payments due under a contract entered into prior to listing, if the contract is related to prohibited goods or services?
qa_pairs.answer: A designated individual or entity is not allowed to make payments due under a contract entered into prior to listing, if the contract is related to prohibited goods or services, unless the CNO has determined that the contract is not related to any of the prohibited goods, services, technologies, or activities, under this Act, or under the United Nations (Security Council) Act, 1947 or any other relevant Act for the time being in force, or by an order issued under any such Act, in relation to weapons of mass destruction and their delivery systems.

qa_pairs.question: What is the time limit for the MEA to submit prior notification to the UNSC or its Committee for making or receiving payments or unfreezing funds?
qa_pairs.answer: The MEA must submit prior notification to the UNSC or its Committee, of the intention to make or receive such payments or to authorise, where appropriate, the unfreezing of funds, other financial assets or economic resources, ten working days prior to such authorization.

qa_pairs.question: What must the RE/Registrar of Immovable Properties/ROC/Regulator and the State Nodal Officer do when an application is received?
qa_pairs.answer: The RE/Registrar of Immovable Properties/ROC/Regulator and the State Nodal Officer shall inform, and forward a copy of the application, together with full details of the asset frozen, as given by applicant to the CNO by email, FAX and by Post, within two working days.

qa_pairs.question: What is the time limit for the CNO to pass an order unfreezing the assets?
qa_pairs.answer: The CNO shall pass an order, without delay, unfreezing the funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services, owned/held by such applicant, within 5 working days.

qa_pairs.question: Under what conditions is it not possible for the CNO to pass an order unfreezing the assets within 5 working days?
qa_pairs.answer: If it is not possible, for any reason, to pass an Order unfreezing the assets within 5 working days, the CNO shall inform the applicant expeditiously.

qa_pairs.question: Who qualifies as a listed person or entity that may petition a request for delisting at the Focal Point Mechanism established under UNSC Resolution?
qa_pairs.answer: Listed persons and entities may petition a request for delisting at the Focal Point Mechanism established under UNSC Resolution.

qa_pairs.question: What is the procedure for an individual/entity to move an application for unfreezing of funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services?
qa_pairs.answer: An individual/entity, if it has evidence to prove that the freezing of funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services, owned/held has been inadvertently frozen, an application may be moved giving the requisite evidence, in writing, to the relevant RE/Registrar of Immovable Properties/ROC/Regulator and the State.

qa_pairs.question: What evidence must an individual/entity provide to support their application for unfreezing of funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services?
qa_pairs.answer: An individual/entity must provide evidence to prove that the freezing of funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services, owned/held has been inadvertently frozen.

qa_pairs.question: What must the CNO do if it is satisfied with the evidence furnished by the individual/entity?
qa_pairs.answer: The CNO shall pass an order, without delay, unfreezing the funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services, owned/held by such applicant, under intimation to all RE/Registrar of Immovable Properties/ROC/Regulators and the State Nodal Officer.

qa_pairs.question: What is the basis for the CNO to pass an order unfreezing the funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services?

qa_pairs.question: What are the simplified KYC norms for small accounts?
qa_pairs.answer: Under paragraph 23 of Chapter VI, when an individual without an OVD desires to open a bank account, banks shall open a Small Account with the following limitations: (i) aggregate credits in a financial year must not exceed Rs. 1 lakh; (ii) aggregate withdrawals/transfers in a month must not exceed Rs. 10,000; (iii) balance at any point must not exceed Rs. 50,000 (this limit does not apply to deposits via Government grants or welfare benefits). Conditions: (a) The bank shall obtain a self-attested photograph from the customer. (b) The designated bank officer shall certify under signature that the person affixed signature or thumb impression in his presence. Small accounts are initially valid for 12 months; they may continue for another 12 months if the account holder applies for an OVD. After 24 months, the account ceases to be operational until full CDD is complete. Foreign remittances cannot be credited to a small account.
